《字林西报》，1936年11月13日，星期五
1749

棉纺厂
前线平静
但气氛紧张

警察预备队
待命以防
骚乱

小规模骚乱
迅速被制止

公大第三厂关闭；
怡和纱厂
重新开工

尽管昨天下午日本纱厂区的局势依然紧张，但自清晨杨树浦路540号公大二厂发生事件以来，怠工工人未再试图采取暴力行动。

随着暮色笼罩这一动荡地区，杨树浦警方报告称局势平静，但预备队仍严阵以待，以防进一步麻烦。日本水兵也在停工及仍在运营的纱厂外站岗放哨。

位于腾越路195号的达康纺织公司纱厂于昨天上午停工，从而使怠工工人总数从8,000人回升至10,000人。据报，平凉路和杨树浦路上的公大公司丝厂工人也情绪不稳，但这未能得到证实。公司官员宣称，这两家工厂正满负荷运转。

拒绝工作

位于腾越路的达康纱厂是周二晚罢工纠察队与警察发生冲突的地点，该厂周三夜间无法运营，仅有250名夜班工人报到上班。公司官员派卡车前往公司华员宿舍，欲接来约1,000名需上夜班的工人。工人们断然拒绝前往，称其领班已受到警告，若去上班将被杀害。

东洋纺织株式会社（Tokwa Boseki Kaisha）昨天下午报告称，自周三以来，其几乎70%的工人已恢复工作。位于杨树浦路的东华纱厂（Dong Shing Spinning and Weaving Company）的罢工者已接受公司提出的加薪5%的条件，并于昨晚到岗上班。

公大二厂的麻烦始于昨天凌晨3点左右，当时30名年轻女孩进入厂区并开始高呼口号。她们成功煽动约200名女纺纱工和织布工陷入狂热，随后骚乱真正爆发。

随之发生小规模骚乱

在警察控制事态之前，机器停止运转，筒管被扔得满地都是，30扇窗户被砸碎。警方在处理局势时设法避免了暴力，但在驱散人群之前，有必要从榆林路巡捕房调出额外巡逻队。

当厂区恢复平静时，约720名夜班工人已离岗，口头要求加薪20%。到早上6点，罢工者已离开厂区，管理层于7点关闭了工厂。该厂目前仍处于关闭状态。

位于杨树浦路670号的老怡和纱厂于昨天重新开工，该厂曾于今年1月16日关闭，这显示了杨树浦趋向和平的趋势。该厂昨天上午招收了约1,000名工人。

船津指责缺乏诉求

据《上海每日新闻》昨天报道，在华日本棉纺业同业公会会长船津辰一郎（Tatsuichiro Funatsu）先生在接受大上海市政府社会局代表采访时，批评了中国工人在日本纱厂罢工前未提出诉求的做法。

“我告知中国官员，有三家工人罢工的纱厂已同意加薪5%，”引文称船津先生说。“我还指出，罢工者在未提出诉求的情况下就停工或‘消极怠工’是极不规范的。我们认为，罢工者先提出诉求才是公平的，如果资方拒绝，他们再采取认为合适的措施。如果劳方先罢工再提诉求，就不能指望劳资开明关系的健康发展。

“值得注意的是，尽管日本纱厂因抵制运动遭受严重损失，但它们支付给中国工人的工资仍与五年前相同。此外，还有许多中国纱厂已经关闭，另一些则仅部分时间运营。考虑到这一点，在日本纱厂工作的中国劳工是幸运的。我请中国官员向工人传达这些观点。”

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, November 11, 1936

All Quiet Along
Factory Front,
Work Resuming

Rioter Given Prison
Term; Police Keep
Close Watch

CHINESE POLICE
BREAK UP PARADE

Situation Still Tense
With Many Workers
Holding Ground

Indicative of the general quiet and lack of outside influences along the Yangtzepoo Mill Front, 2500 workers of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, who yesterday were besieged by a gang of about 5000 strikers attempting to get them to join the strike, quietly trooped into work last night and this morning and the mill reports that a full complement of workers is on hand. The workers are asking for a 10 per cent increase in wages; the management has countered with an offer of a five per cent raise.

Responsible officials pointed out this morning that though there were a great many mill employees on strike, the situation could by no means be regarded as serious and that the critical trouble which arose at this time last year was definitely not expected, principally because of the fact that no motives other than that of an increase of pay was behind the strike. In last years' trouble outside agencies had stirred the workers to strike.

Return To Jobs

Reports from Japanese mills this morning showed workers returning to their jobs in normal fashion. From the Tung Wah Mill at 7 o'clock came the word that 1000 workers had returned and the situation was described as "normal." The night workers of the Shanghai No. 6 Mill reported for duty quietly last night.

At the Mei Wha Dyeing Factory 110 male workers and 20 females are asking for a five per cent increase and double pay for overtime. An hour's lunch period is also being requested with a 10 per cent salary for this period.

Drawing an unusually stiff sentence, Sze Vee-ziang, arrested yesterday during the height of the disturbances outside the Dah Kong Mill, was sentenced to eight months' imprisonment this morning by Judge Tsoong in the First District Court. Detective Sub-Inspector Crighton attached to Yulin Road Police Station appeared in the witness box with his arm in a sling and related how he had ridden his motorcycle through the crowd in order to break it up when about 10 or 20 persons had begun stoning him. He suffered injuries to his arm, hand and nose. One of the stoners, who hit Crighton with his missiles, was arrested by a Japanese policeman and sentenced this morning.

Mills Resume Work

With Japanese naval patrols and details of Shanghai Municipal Police guarding the approaches to the plant, the 1300 girl operatives of the Tokwa Boseki Kaisha, Ward Road, at 6 o'clock this morning quietly trooped into the mill and resumed work. The majority of them had gone on strike on Monday demanding increased wages.

This development came as a surprise, as a further spread of the strike in Japanese-owned mills was generally expected following the picketing of the gates of the Dah Kong Mill by strikers yesterday evening.

No Concessions Made

According to officials of the Tokya Boseki Kaishi, the workers resumed work voluntarily, no concessions having been made to the demands of labor by the company.

The strike and subsequent lock-out enforced by the employers, assertedly to prevent the destruction of equipment, this morning had narrowed down to the five plants of the Shanghai Cotton Manufacturing Co. and the two mills of the Dong Shing Spinning and Weaving Co., Yangtzepoo Road.

8000 Idle

Company estimates placed the number of workers still idle at about 8000.

Reached over the telephone, a Dong Shing spokesman said that the main difficulty in reaching an agreement with the workers was the latter's lack of duly elected official representatives.

This phenomenon, he added was common in cases of labor unrest among Chinese. Fear that they might be "blacklisted" and consequently lose their jobs prevented the leaders of the movement to come out and speak on behalf of others, he alleged. His firm, the spokesman continued, was still ready to increase wages by 5 per cent against the 20 per cent demanded in handbills allegedly distributed by strikers.

March Broken Up

Declaring that a girl worker is missing since the disturbances in front of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, 2533 Yangtzepoo Road, last night, and seeking official support for their demands to increase their wages, about 1000 mill hands marched on Huang Shing Road this morning in an attempt to stage a demonstration in front of the City Government of Greater Shanghai and its Bureau of Social Affairs.

Prepared for all eventualities, a combined force of Bureau of Public Safety officers and the Settlement police halted the marchers and dispersed them after some minor clashes. A delegation of 13, however, was permitted to proceed to the Bureau of Social Affairs under police escort to present their case.

Plans Fail

Leaders of the striking mill workers had originally hoped to mobilize a force of 20,000 strikers to stage the parade and demonstration. The plan, however, did not materialize and only about 1000 turned up for the march. They started from the Yangtzepoo district near the boundary of the Chinese territory and marched on Huang Shing Road which leads to the Civic Center, only to be blocked by the officers.

All was quiet on the Yangtzepoo strike front today following trouble last night in the district. However, no settlement between the Japanese mill owners and the strikers materialized and the situation still remains threatening, as the workers are apparently firm in their stand. Apart from the reinforced police vigilance and Japanese Marine sentries with sub-machine guns stationed at various points in the Yangtzepoo district, the situation was calm and few bands of idle workers could be seen around the district.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年11月11日，星期三

工厂前线
一片平静，
工作恢复

骚乱者被判
监禁；警方
严密监视

中国警察
驱散游行

局势依然紧张
许多工人
坚持立场

显示杨树浦纱厂前线总体平静且无外部势力影响的是，达康棉纺厂的2,500名工人昨天被一群约5,000名试图拉他们加入罢工的罢工者围困，但他们于昨晚和今晨安静地列队进厂上班，该厂报告称工人已全部到岗。工人们要求加薪10%；管理层则以加薪5%作为回应。

负责官员今天上午指出，尽管有大量纱厂员工罢工，但局势绝不能被视为严重，而且去年此时出现的危急麻烦肯定不在预期之内，主要是因为这次罢工背后除了加薪之外没有其他动机。去年的麻烦中，有外部机构煽动工人罢工。

重返岗位

今天早晨来自日本纱厂的报告显示，工人正正常返回工作岗位。同华纱厂在7点钟传来消息，称1,000名工人已返回，局势被描述为“正常”。上海第六纱厂的夜班工人昨晚安静地报到上班。

在美华印染厂，110名男工和20名女工要求加薪5%以及加班费加倍。他们还要求有一小时的午餐时间，并在此期间支付10%的薪水。

施维江（Sze Vee-ziang，音译）在昨天达康纱厂外骚乱最激烈时被捕，今天上午在第一特区法院被宗法官判处八个月监禁，量刑异常严厉。隶属于榆林路巡捕房的副督察克里顿（Crighton）手臂吊着绷带出现在证人席上，讲述了当他骑摩托车穿过人群以驱散人群时，约有10或20人开始向他投掷石块。他的手臂、手和鼻子受伤。其中一名用石块击中克里顿的投石者被一名日本警察逮捕，并于今天上午被判刑。

纱厂恢复工作

在日本海军巡逻队和公共租界工部局警务处分队守卫工厂通道的情况下，位于华德路的东洋纺织株式会社（Tokwa Boseki Kaisha）的1,300名女工于今晨6点安静地列队进入纱厂并恢复工作。她们中的大多数人曾在周一罢工，要求增加工资。

这一发展令人意外，因为继昨天傍晚罢工者在达康纱厂门口设立纠察线后，人们普遍预计日本拥有的纱厂罢工将进一步蔓延。

未作让步

据东洋纺织株式会社（Tokya Boseki Kaishi，原文拼写有误，应为Tokwa）官员称，工人是自愿恢复工作的，公司并未对劳工的要求作出任何让步。

罢工及随后雇主为防止设备破坏而实施的闭厂，今天上午已缩小至上海纺织株式会社的五家工厂和位于杨树浦路的东华纺织印染公司的两家纱厂。

8,000人闲置

公司估计仍在闲置的工人人数约为8,000人。

通过电话采访，东华公司的一位发言人表示，与工人达成协议的主要困难在于后者缺乏正式选举产生的官方代表。

他补充说，这种现象在中国人的劳工动荡案件中很常见。他声称，由于担心被列入“黑名单”从而失去工作，运动的领导人不敢站出来为他人代言。这位发言人继续说，他的公司仍愿意加薪5%，以应对据称由罢工者散发的传单中要求的20%加薪。

游行被驱散

声称自昨晚杨树浦路2533号达康棉纺厂前的骚乱以来有一名女工失踪，并寻求官方支持其加薪要求，约1,000名纱厂工人今天上午向黄兴路进发，试图在大上海市政府及其社会局前举行示威。

公共安全局警官和租界警察组成的联合部队为应对各种可能发生的情况，阻止了游行队伍，并在发生一些小冲突后将其驱散。然而，一个由13人组成的代表团在警察护送下获准前往社会局陈述案情。

计划失败

罢工纱厂工人的领导人最初希望动员20,000名罢工者举行游行和示威。然而，该计划未能实现，只有约1,000人参加游行。他们从中国领土边界附近的杨树浦地区出发，向通往市中心（Civic Center）的黄兴路进发，结果被警官们阻挡。

继该地区昨晚发生麻烦后，今天杨树浦罢工前线一切平静。然而，日本纱厂主与罢工者之间并未达成和解，局势仍然具有威胁性，因为工人们显然立场坚定。除了加强警察警戒以及在杨树浦区各要点部署配备冲锋枪的日本海军陆战队哨兵外，局势平静，在该地区周围很少能看到成群的 idle workers（怠工工人）。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 12, 1936

SHANGHAI MILL STRIKE
The current unrest among Chinese workers in the cotton mills of Shanghai is one of those pieces of opportunism in which those who direct labour's interests are always prone to indulge. After many months of slack trade, during which only part time has been worked and some of the Chinese-owned mills have been forced to close down, a sudden "boom" in the spinning and weaving industry is now being enjoyed. A good many mills being at full output. Labour organisers have seen in this fact an opportunity to demand higher pay for the workers and, beginning in a small way about a week ago, there is now a considerable number of workers disaffected. It is interesting to note that trouble first started in Chinese-owned mills, about 5,000 workers in the employ of various firms staging a "go-slow" strike. It was later reported that this difficulty had been settled by the owners agreeing to a ten per cent. wages increase, and it was following this that the trouble spread to Japanese-owned mills in which handbills were distributed demanding a 20 per cent. increase and other improvements in conditions. It is here that one sees the hand of the political agitator, for there are accusations made against the Japanese managements of "brutality" by overseers, as well as other unjustified charges. There are several thousands of employees affected and it is known that a considerable amount of pressure and intimidation is being applied, as was evidenced by the serious misbehaviour of a crowd outside the Dah Kong Mill on Tuesday evening, when a crowd of over 1,000 men and girl strikers from other mills demonstrated to compel those who preferred to remain at work joining in the stoppage. Fortunately, there was no very untoward development and it is to be hoped that moderating counsel will be given the strike leaders and that the police will be able to afford the fullest protection to mill property and also to those workers who desire to go about their peaceful labours. The Japanese millowners have offered reinstatement to all workers and a five per cent. increase in wages, but as this has been refused it is time for further negotiations, not for brickbats.
It is the nature of the demonstration against the Japanese mills which justifies the Japanese contention that there is Communistic and political influence at the back of the particularization which Japanese mills are now suffering. One cannot condemn workers who seek to improve their working conditions by peaceful means, for all men have the right to sell their labour as profitably as they can and to withhold it if conditions are lower than they have a right to expect. But that is something far different from political agitation, and it is most seriously to be hoped that Chinese leaders in this area will realize the necessity of doing everything possible to prevent a political complexion being given to what started as an ordinary labour dispute. It must be remembered that a vast investment is represented by Japanese cotton mills here, that they have provided thousands of workers with a better livelihood than they would otherwise have obtained, and that, because of efficient management and modern machinery, they have been employing workers when a good many of the Chinese mills could not. It also has to be noted that the demands in the case of the Japanese mills are higher than were advanced to Chinese employers. At the moment, the strike cannot be regarded as having grown to really serious proportions but there are about thirty Japanese cotton mills of varying size in this district and the livelihood of a great many operatives would be affected if matters were allowed to develop. It is a pity, too, that the revival of business is being threatened just at a time when conditions generally promise to improve, and all who have the welfare of Shanghai at heart must be hoping that an agreement will be quickly and amicably reached.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年11月12日，星期四

上海纱厂罢工

目前上海华资棉纺厂中国工人的动荡局势，是那些主导劳工利益者总是倾向于利用的机会主义行径之一。在经历了数月的贸易萧条之后——在此期间仅实行部分工时，且部分华资纱厂被迫关闭——纺纱和织布行业如今正享受着一阵突如其来的“繁荣”。许多纱厂已满负荷生产。劳工组织者视此事实为要求提高工人工资的契机，约于一周前小规模开始，如今已有相当数量的工人心生不满。值得注意的是，麻烦最初始于华资纱厂，受雇于各家公司的约5,000名工人举行了“怠工”罢工。随后有报道称，资方同意加薪百分之十，从而解决了这一困难；此后，事态蔓延至日资纱厂，那里散发了传单，要求加薪百分之二十并改善其他工作条件。在此可以看到政治煽动者的黑手，因为有人指控日本管理层存在监工“残暴”行为以及其他毫无根据的指责。受影响雇员达数千人，众所周知，当局施加了相当大的压力和恐吓，周二晚上大康纱厂（Dah Kong Mill）外人群的严重不当行为即为明证，当时来自其他纱厂的1,000多名男女罢工者示威，强迫那些宁愿继续工作的工人加入停工行列。幸运的是，并未发生非常不利的演变，希望有人能向罢工领导人提供温和的建议，也希望警方能够为纱厂财产以及那些希望从事和平劳动的工人提供最充分的保护。日本纱厂主已提出恢复所有工人的工作并加薪百分之五，但由于这一提议被拒绝，现在是进行进一步谈判的时候，而不是扔砖头的时候。

正是针对日资纱厂的示威性质，证明了日方的主张是正确的，即日本纱厂目前遭受的特定困境背后存在着共产主义和政治影响。人们不能谴责那些通过和平手段寻求改善工作条件的工人，因为所有人都有权尽可能有利地出卖自己的劳动力，并在条件低于其有权期望的水平时拒绝提供劳动力。但这与政治煽动截然不同，我们最诚挚地希望该地区的中国领导人认识到，必须尽一切可能防止这场起初仅为普通劳资纠纷的事件带上政治色彩。必须记住，日本的棉纺厂在这里代表了巨大的投资，它们为成千上万的工人提供了比否则所能获得的更好的生计，而且由于管理高效和机器现代化，在许多华资纱厂无法雇佣工人的时候，它们仍在雇佣工人。还须注意，针对日资纱厂提出的要求高于向华资雇主提出的要求。目前，罢工的规模尚不能被视为已发展到真正严重的程度，但该地区约有三十家规模不一的日本棉纺厂，如果事态任其发展，许多操作工的生计将受到影响。令人遗憾的是，就在总体形势有望好转之际，商业复苏却受到威胁，所有关心上海福祉的人都希望尽快达成友好协议。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No 238/36.
D. 7599
Pootoo Road Station,
REPORT
Date. 26.11.36.

Subject Notices posted in all Japanese Mills in Pootoo Road District
by Mill Management.

Made by D.S.I. Burton. Forwarded by O. S. Polkern Inspecr

Sir,

Posters about 3 feet square and written in Chinese ink
have been posted at all Japanese owned mills in the Pootoo Road
District, this a.m., by the Mill Managements, a copy of the
translation is hereunder recorded:-

1. According to the anouncement made during last week, the
workers will be given a wage increase of 5%. (Those workers whose
wages are too low will be given a larger proportional increase).
This system will be carried into effect after the 15th of November
1936.

2. Due to corruption, the bonus system for each month
will not be restored. However, it will be replaced by the reward
system, namely, those workers whose work is very good will be
rewarded with a wage increase and class promotion.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH / SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 26 NOV 1936）

3. There will be 12 hours work for Sundays. If the workers
do more than 12 hours on Sundays, they will be given extra pay
and one meal. Those who do not wish to work more than 12 hours
need not do so.

D.S. 48 Mori received information from Mr. Kamada of
the Personnel Department, N.W.K. No. 1 & 2 Mills, that these
posters have been drawn up as a result of a conference held by
Mr. Funatsu, President of the Japanese Mills Association of China
and Mr. Doo Yoch Sung (杜月笙) at about 8 p.m. on the 25.11.36.,
place where conference was held was unknown.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
（签名）
D.S.I.

（批：DAR / 26/11）

INTELLIGENCE

杂项档案第238/36号。
D. 7599
普陀路捕房，
报告
日期：1936年11月26日。

主题：普陀路地区所有日资纱厂由厂方张贴的告示。

由分区督察伯顿（Burton）撰写。经警司波尔肯（Polkern）转发

先生，

今晨，普陀路地区所有日资纱厂均由厂方张贴了约3英尺见方、用墨笔书写的中文海报，译文副本记录如下：-

1. 根据上周发布的公告，工人将获得5%的工资增加。（工资过低的工人将获得更大比例的增加）。此制度将于1936年11月15日后生效。

2. 由于存在腐败现象，每月奖金制度将不予恢复。然而，将以奖励制度取而代之，即工作表现极佳的工人将获得加薪和职级晋升。

（印：特别股 / 上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1936年11月26日）

3. 周日工作时间为12小时。如果工人在周日工作超过12小时，将获得额外报酬和一餐饭食。不愿工作超过12小时者无需如此。

D.S. 48 Mori 从日华纱厂第一、二厂人事部的 Kamada 先生处获悉，这些海报是1936年11月25日晚8时许，由在华日资纱厂协会会长船津先生（Funatsu）与杜月笙先生开会后拟定的，会议地点不详。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）
分区督察

（批：DAR / 11月26日）

REPORT
Date November 25, 1936.

Subject Japan-China Nos.5, 6 and 7 Cotton Mills (Kiwa)
- Dispute over dismissal of caterers.

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by Chimoore A.S.I.

In connection with the dispute among the workers
of the Japan-China Nos.5, 6 and 7 Cotton Mills (Kiwa),
74 Robison Road, O.O.L., as a result of the dismissal of
six caterers, it is reported that the following terms were
agreed upon by the management and the employees during a
meeting held, under the auspices of an official of the
Bureau of Social Affairs, at 3 p.m. November 23 on the
mill premises :-

1. That a 5% wage increase be granted to the workers.
2. That half an hour rest be granted to the employees
during tiffin (from 12 noon to 12.30 p.m.).
3. That the demands for the issue of rice allowance and
the restoration of monthly bonus be referred to the
Japanese Cotton Mill Owners' Federation.
4. That the working period for Sundays be not extended
after 9 a.m.
5. That new employees required by the management be
recruited from unemployed workers living in the
workers' quarters.
6. That no workers be dismissed and that no caterers be
forced to evacuate the workers' quarters.
7. That the six dismissed caterers be reinstated and/permitted to live
in the workers' quarters.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 25 NOV 1936）

Sih Tse liang

由督察员 Sih Tse-liang（音译）撰写，由助理副督察长 Chimoore（音译）转呈

鉴于罗宾森路74号（外侨居留地）日华纱厂第五、六、七厂（喜和）工人因六名炊事员被解雇而发生纠纷，据报，在11月23日下午3时于厂区内在社会局官员的主持下召开的会议上，资方与雇员达成了以下条款：-

1. 给予工人5%的工资增加。

6. 不得解雇任何工人，也不得强迫任何炊事员撤离工人宿舍区。
7. 六名被解雇的炊事员应复职并/或允许居住在工人宿舍区。

Subject Kiwa Cotton Mill Strikers' Demands submitted to the Bureau
of Social Affairs and accepted by Mill Management.

Made by. D.S.I.Burton. Forwarded by. O - A Perkins Insp.

Sir,

At 8 a.m. 23.11.36., 10 representatives namely:-
1. Chow Dau Sung (周道生) 6. Yue Seu Van (于守藩)
2. Ho Han Sz (何漢如) 7. Sung Ling Sui (孫林瑞)
3. Lee Pau Zien (李寶全) 8. Yoh S Ling (岳士林)
4. Zung Koh Yue (陳國餘) 9. Wong Han (王漢)
5. Sung Tuh Kyung (孫德金) 10. Ching Sung Pau (鄭生保)

of Kiwa Cotton Mill, No.74 Robison Road, O.O.L., proceeded to the
Bureau of Social Affairs, Kiangwan, where they were interviewed by
Mr. Wong Ping, Officer i/c the 3rd Division Social Affairs. These
representatives submitted 7 demands:-

1. Wage increase of 5%.
2. Machines to be stopped for 30 minutes during meal
times.
3. Rice bonus to be put on the same basis as that of
the N.W.K. Mills.
4. All extra work to cease at 9 a.m. on Sundays.
5. When new workers are wanted the management to employ
workers living in the mill quarters first.
6. No workers to be dismissed without good reason, and
no food contractors to be ejected from the mill premises.
7. The 6 dismissed food contractors to be reinstated.

Mr. Wong Ping promised the representatives that he
would take the demands up with the Mill Management and accordingly
at 3 p.m. 23.11.36., Mr. Wong Ping, Col. Tan Pau Zeu, Officer i/c
6th Division, P.S.B. and Mr. Liang Foo Tsoo (梁扶初), Officer i/c
4th Division, P.S.B., held a conference with 2 members of the
mill management, Mr. Korogi and Mr. Yoshitomi, when after a long
discussion, the mill management accepted the workers' demands.

1936年11月23日上午8时，位于外马路罗便臣道74号的日华纱厂10名代表，即：
1. 周道生 (Chow Dau Sung)    6. 于守藩 (Yue Seu Van)

2. 用餐时间停机30分钟。

Date November 23, 1936.

Subject Japan-China Nos.5, 6 and 7 Cotton Mills (Kiwa), 74 Robison
Road, O.O.L. - Agitation re dismissal of six caterers
Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by Kilmoore A.C.P.

At 10 a.m. November 23, eighteen caterers of the
Japan-China Nos.5, 6 and 7 (Kiwa) Cotton Mills, 74 Robison
Road, O.O.L. appealed for assistance to the Bureau of Social
Affairs in securing the reinstatement of the six caterers
who were dismissed on November 22. The callers were
received by Wong Sien-tsing (王先青), an official of
the Mediation Department of the Bureau, who promised to
take up the matter.

It is reported that following a discussion which
took place in a food shop between 12 noon and 2 p.m.
November 23 the caterers decided to urge the management to
re-engage their six dismissed colleagues, and if this demand
is ignored, to request all workers to resign and withdraw
their deposits from the mill. It was further decided that
in every ten workers' quarters of the mills, two caterers
be held responsible for preventing workers therein from
resuming operations.

There are some 2,000 workers living in the 300
quarters of these mills.

（左侧批注：In Chinese dist. Div?）

Sih Tse Liang
D. I.

事由：外马路罗便臣道74号日华第五、六、七纱厂（Kiwa）——关于解雇六名伙食承包商的煽动活动
呈报人：督察席子良（Sih Tse-liang） 转呈人：副总巡基尔莫尔（Kilmoore）

11月23日上午10时，位于外马路罗便臣道74号的日华第五、六、七（日华）纱厂的18名伙食承包商向社会局求助，要求恢复11月22日被解雇的6名伙食承包商的职务。来访者由该局调解科官员王先青（Wong Sien-tsing）接待，他承诺处理此事。

据报，在11月23日中午12时至下午2时之间，伙食承包商们在一家饭馆进行讨论后，决定敦促管理层重新雇用其六名被解雇的同事；如果这一要求被忽视，则请求所有工人辞职并从工厂提取存款。此外还决定，在工厂每十个工人宿舍中，由两名伙食承包商负责阻止其中的工人复工。

这些工厂的300间宿舍中居住着约2,000名工人。

（左侧批注：在华界分区？）

contractors namely:-

(3) Chow Dau Sung (周道生).

(5) Lee Pau Hien (李宝金).

were dismissed and must therefore remove from the mill premises
by 25.11.36.

employed at the Kiwa Cotton Mill including the six who have been
dismissed, held a meeting in a small primary school attached to
the mill quarters. Resulting from their deliberations the follow-

(3) A bonus equivalent to two days' wages to be paid
all workers who attend work for a full month without leave.
(4) No workers to be dismissed without justification.
(5) All new employees required to be recruited from the
mill quarters through the agencies of the food contractors.
(6) In order to allow the employees a rest period after
tiffin, all machinery to be stopped for half an hour.
(7) A sum equivalent to 10 per cent of wages to be paid

Sir,
At 8:30 a.m. 20.11.36., 18 representatives of the
Strike Committee of the Kiwa Cotton Mill, No.74 Robison Road,
O.O.L., proceeded to the Bureau of Social Affairs at the City
Government Headquarters, Kiangwan, where they were interviewed
by Wong Sien Ching (王先青) and submitted to him 6 demands as
follows:-
1. Workers whose wages are lower than 50 cents per day
to receive an increase of 15%. workers whose wages are over 50
cents per day to receive an increase of 10%.
2. Amount of wages due to workers to be entered clearly
in the wage book.
3. The machines to be stopped for one hour during meal
times.
4. No workers to be dismissed without just cause, and
no workers to be cruelly treated.
5. Sunday to be treated as a holiday and no extra work
to be done.
6. That a bonus equal to 4 days' wages be granted all
workers each month.
Mr. Wong told the representatives that he would give
the demands due consideration and make enquiries into the
workers' conditions.

I am, Sir,

REPORT
Date 20.11.36.
Subject Strike at the Kiwa Cotton Mill, No.74 Robison Road, O.O.L.
Made by D.S.I.Burton. Forwarded by J. S. Perkins Insp'r

Sir,
At 6:15 p.m. 19.11.36., J.D.S.48 Mori received
information that a strike had been declared at the Kiwa Cotton
Mill, No.74 Robison Road, O.O.L.
Enquiries show that 53 female day shift workers of the
reeling room had gone on strike at 4 p.m. and demanded an increa-
se of wages, at 6 p.m. even date 200 female night shift workers
of the spinning, winding and reeling rooms joined the strike,
those 253 female workers were ejected from the mill by the P.S.
Bureau at 6:30 p.m.. At 7:50 p.m. 930 female night shift workers
of the carding, winding and ring spinning rooms also went on stri-
ke and were ejected from the mill by the P.S. Bureau. The
workers made the following demands.
1. Increase of wages.
2. All workers to receive two days' reward money each
month.
3. Machines to be stopped during meals and 15 minutes
rest to be granted after meals.
4. No workers to be dismissed without just cause.
5. All workers wage books be given them on day before
they are paid to let them know the amount they are to
receive.
The strike effected 312 male night shift workers who had
to cease work as there was nothing for them to do. The mill was
then closed. No trouble was experienced and no demonstrations
made.
At 5:30 a.m. 20.11.36., the mill re-opened and 449 male
and female day shift workers attended and commenced work in the
carding, winding and ring spinning rooms.

D.D.O."B" Div.

由副督察长伯顿（Burton）呈报。经警司珀金斯（J. S. Perkins）转呈

敬启者，
1936年11月19日下午6时15分，日本巡捕第48号森（Mori）接获情报，称位于罗别根路74号（外侨居留地）的吉华纱厂（Kiwa Cotton Mill）已宣布罢工。
经查，缫丝间53名女日班工人于下午4时罢工，要求增加工资；同日傍晚6时，纺纱、络筒及缫丝间的200名女夜班工人加入罢工。上述253名女工于下午6时30分被警务处人员驱逐出厂。晚上7时50分，梳棉、络筒及环锭纺纱间的930名女夜班工人亦举行罢工，并被警务处人员驱逐出厂。工人们提出以下要求：
1. 增加工资。
2. 所有工人每月领取两天的赏金。
3. 用餐期间停机，并在餐后给予15分钟休息时间。
4. 不得无故解雇工人。
5. 在发薪日前一天向所有工人发放工资簿，以便其知晓应得金额。
此次罢工导致312名男夜班工人因无事可做而被迫停工。工厂随后关闭。期间未发生骚乱，亦无示威活动。
1936年11月20日上午5时30分，工厂重新开工，449名男女日班工人到岗，并在梳棉、络筒及环锭纺纱间开始工作。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

At 6 p.m. 17/11/36, the 1st accused in this case was arrested leaving the Dah Kong Cotton Mill Tengyueh Road, with four application forms of the "Shanghai Municipality Textile Trade Employees Mutual Aid Association" along with a fountain pen, concealed inside an electric torch, which he was carrying in his pocket.

This man gave information which led to the arrest of the 2nd accused at 10 p.m. on 17/11/36 at a country house off Limohing Road. When arrested this accused admitted having given these forms to the 1st accused and implicated one named Yang Siau Sei (楊孝先) residing No.9 Chi Shi Li (積善里) Sungpan Road. Endeavours to arrest the man, have to date proved futile.

At 7 p.m. 17/11/36, the 3rd accused was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the circulation of Rice Coupons, and on being questioned admitted the offence, implicating as her instigator the 4th accused, who was arrested at 9 p.m. on 18/11/36 at 1893 Yangtsepoo Road. Both these females implicated as the ringleader one named Ling Kung Dee (林根弟), who to date has not been arrested, owing to her having absconded from her home.

The 1st, 2nd and 3rd accused appeared at S.S.D. Court on the 18/11/36 under a Writ of Detention, as did the 4th accused on the 19/11/36. All were remanded in custody until 25/11/36 for trial.

1936年11月17日下午6时，本案第一被告离开腾越路大康纱厂时被捕，身上藏有四份“上海市纺织业职工互助会”的申请表以及一支藏在手电筒内的钢笔，该手电筒藏于其口袋中。

此人提供的情报导致第二被告于1936年11月17日晚上10时在临清路附近的一处乡间房屋被捕。被捕时，该被告承认曾将这些表格交给第一被告，并供出一名名叫楊孝先（Yang Siau Sei）的人，其居住在宋潘路积善里9号。迄今试图逮捕该人的努力均告失败。

1936年11月17日晚上7时，第三被告因涉嫌参与流通米票而被捕，经讯问后承认罪行，并供出其煽动者为第四被告，后者于1936年11月18日晚上9时在杨树浦路1893号被捕。这两名女性均供认林根弟（Ling Kung Dee）为首领，该人因离家潜逃，迄今尚未被捕。

第一、第二和第三被告于1936年11月18日凭拘留令出庭受审，第四被告于1936年11月19日出庭。所有人均被还押候审，直至1936年11月25日受审。

Sir,
I beg to report that in compliance with instructions
contained on attached report D.S. McKown accompany by the
undersigned visited the Min Ching (青) Primary School,
on the afternoon of the 20/11/36 for the purpose of interviewing
the principal Mr. Chiang Hang Tse (蔣行之) however on
arrival there it was found that he was absent, owing to his t
teaching in the Ming Ts (明志) primary school, situated in
the Ah Tuh Li (阿德里) alleyway, Yangtszepoo Road.
A visit was made to the latter address and an interview
obtained with the person in question, who gave a statement to the
effect, that since taking control of the Min Ching School he had
dismissed nearly all the old teachers who had been responsible
for the bad reputation of the school, and that it was now his
desire to co-operate in every way with the police, in order to
stamp out "Radicalism" amongst his teachers and pupils.
Mr. Chiang, was thanked for his promised co-operation, and
assured that the police would reciprocate to assist him in his
endeavours. It was pointed out to Mr. Chiang, that he must be
careful of the persons attending his evening classes, especially
those from industrial concerns, who might attempt to hold meeting
regarding the present strike situation, and again he promised
that in event of any such thing taking place, he would immediate-
ly report same to the police.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]
D. S. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 578/36.
B. D. 2599
Yulin Road Station, 23 // 36
REPORT
Date. Nov. 23. 19 36.

Subject Further to Labour Situation in Yulin Road District.

Made by D. I. Brownrigg Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
All mills in this district are working normally at 7 a.m.
23-11-36.
S.O. 170 reports having received information that rice could be obtained from the "San Yang" Rice Shop, situated at No. 590-2 Ward Road by the mill workers.
Later the said C.D.C. went to the rice shop and ascertained that on 14th and 16th Nov. 1936, a male Chinese, age about 30, medium build, wearing black cotton long gown, speaking Shanghai dialect, bought 300 and 400 tickets for rice, (100 tickets for 1/5th of a peck and other 300 tickets for 1/10th of a peck).
The Old Ewo Mill No. 1056 Yangtsepoo Road, opened this morning at 7 a.m. employing 1005 workers on day and night shifts. No trouble on opening, but rumours received that some of the workers who formerly worked there, but have not been re-engaged might cause trouble later in the day.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. I.

(印：23 NOV 1936)

D. D. O. "Jr".

D.C. (Spl. Br.)

INTELLIGENCE REPORT

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 578/36。
B. D. 2599
榆林路巡捕房, 1936年 // 23日
报告
日期. 1936年11月23日。

事由 关于榆林路辖区劳工局势的后续情况。

呈报人 警司布朗里格 (Brownrigg) 转呈人 [签名]

先生，
1936年11月23日上午7时，本辖区所有纱厂均正常开工。
170号巡佐报告称收到消息，纱厂工人可从位于华德路590-2号的“三阳”米店获得大米。
随后，该刑事侦缉处长前往该米店，查明1936年11月14日和16日，一名约30岁、中等身材、身穿黑色棉长袍、讲上海话的中国男子购买了300张和400张米票（100张为五分之一斗，另300张为十分之一斗）。
杨树浦路1056号的老怡和纱厂今早7时开工，昼夜班共雇佣105名工人。开工时未发生骚乱，但收到谣言称，一些此前在该厂工作但未被重新雇佣的工人可能会在当天晚些时候制造麻烦。

此致，
敬礼，
[签名]
警司。

(印：1936年11月23日)

“Jr”区副督察长。

特别课警司。

情报报告

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 282/36.
Yangtzepoo Station,
Further REPORT
Date Nov. 23rd. 19 36.
Subject
Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [签名] Inspt. O. i/c
Sir,
I beg to report, that at 6.10 p.m. 22/11/36, simultaneously to the arrest of Duen Nyi Ling (段義林) now detained under Writ of Detention No. 6/36 Yangtzepoo, another male Chinese named Zee Siao Sz Tz (徐小四子) age 24, native of Yangchow, residing country house, Chaoyang Road, near Meichow Road, was also brought to station for enquiries, as it was suspected that he also was concerned in the agitation of workers, particulary so, when he appears on Special Branch S 1 Report on suspected agitators dated 13/11/36.
This man was subject to a lengthy and strict interrogation, but nothing of an incriminating nature could be found against him, also a search of his home revealed nothing.
In view of aforegoing, he was, after being cautioned to cease any activities that he might have previously been concerned in, allowed to go.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[签名]
D. S. I.
D.D.O. "D"
Copy forwarded to i/c Spl. Brh.

先生，
谨此报告，1936年11月22日下午6时10分，在逮捕段義林 (Duen Nyi Ling) 的同时（现根据杨树浦第6/36号拘留令被拘留），另一名名为徐小四子 (Zee Siao Sz Tz) 的中国男子也被带至巡捕房接受问询，此人24岁，扬州人，居住在朝阳路近梅周路的乡间房屋，因涉嫌参与煽动工人，特别是鉴于其出现在1936年11月13日关于嫌疑煽动者的特别课 S 1 报告中。
对该人进行了长时间且严格的审讯，但未发现任何对其不利的罪证，对其住所的搜查也未发现任何可疑物品。
鉴于上述情况，在警告其停止此前可能参与的任何活动后，准予其离开。
此致，
敬礼，
[签名]
副巡官。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 9 a.m. 19/11/36, the 4th accused Wong Al Pau ( 王亞保 ) appeared at above Court, and after a preliminary hearing, during the course of which she admitted having given the 3rd accused a Rice Coupon, she was remanded in custody until the 25/11/36, when she would appear with the 1st, 2nd and 3rd accused.

During the period of remand, all four accused were subject to a lengthy interrogation and as a result made written statements (copies attached) in which they admit playing active parts during the recent strike movement.

The 1st accused, in his written statement, admits, that knowing he was doing wrong, he accepted from the 2nd accused five "Mutual Aid Society" application forms, and that his intention was to circulate same amongst the employees of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, with the idea of again bringing them out on strike, after the original strike for an increase of wages, had been amicably settled between the management and the workers, the latter having resumed work without further trouble on the 13/11/36.

of Rice Tickets to workers is done somewhat on the same

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong Piao Mei,
native of Soochow, taken by me Makcryn D.S.
at Y'poo Sta., on the 20/11/36, and interpreted by

My name is Wong Piao Mei, native of Soochow, age 24.
I reside with my mother and my husband named Wong Kwei Sung
at No. 87 Tung Zung Li, Tseu Ko Za Road. I was born in
Shanghai and have never been to school. I married in 1932.
In the Autumn of 1929 I obtained a post as an apprentice in
the San Sing Cotton Mill. One year later, I joined the
Dong Shing Cotton Mill and worked in the Fine Yarn Room for
three years. Owing to illness I resigned from the Dong Shing
Mill in May 1933, but subsequently joined the Shanghai Cotton
Mill No. 2 where I worked for two years. Owing to a reduction
in staff I was dismissed in June 1935, and I then re-joined
the Dong Shing Cotton Mill. In February 1936, one named
Siao Ning Po joined the waste cotton picking room and in about
August, one named Kang Di joined my room. We then became
acquainted. About one week before the declaration of the
strike, Kang Di secretly told me that workers of other
Japanese mills had struck work to enforce a demand for an
increase in wages and that we should do likewise. At the
time Siao Ning Po did not say anything to me. On November 8,
when I reported for duty at 6 p.m. I found that a strike had
been declared in the weaving room of the mill. When the
manager announced to the workers that an increase of 5% would
be granted. All workers however insisted on 10%. So we
all left the mill.
About three days after the strike, I met Kang Di in the
Tung Zung Li alleyway and she advised me to persist in the
strike and follow others in the movement. She then left.

以下是由我，副警司 Makcryn，于1936年11月20日在杨树浦警局录取，并由……翻译的苏州籍女子黄飘梅的供词。

我叫黄飘梅，苏州人，24岁。我与母亲和丈夫黄桂生住在曹家渡路同宗里87号。我出生在上海，从未上过学。我于1932年结婚。1929年秋，我在三星纱厂获得学徒职位。一年后，我加入东兴纱厂，在细纱间工作了三年。由于生病，我于1933年5月从东兴纱厂辞职，但随后加入上海第二棉纺厂，工作了两年。由于裁员，我于1935年6月被解雇，随后重新加入东兴纱厂。1936年2月，一名叫萧宁波的人加入废棉挑选间，大约8月，一名叫康弟的人加入我的车间。我们由此相识。在宣布罢工前约一周，康弟秘密告诉我，其他日本纱厂的工人为了要求增加工资而罢工，我们也应该这样做。当时萧宁波没有对我说什么。11月8日，当我下午6点上班时，发现工厂织布间已宣布罢工。当经理向工人宣布将加薪5%时。所有工人都坚持要求10%。于是我们都离开了工厂。
罢工大约三天后，我在同宗里弄堂遇到康弟，她劝我坚持罢工，跟随其他人参与运动。然后她就走了。

On the following day, when I was knitting in the alleyway
with two neighbours, Siao Ning Po appeared in the alleyway
and commenced talking with her as those on the labour situation
remarking that all Chinese should unite together and that the
Japanese always treated Chinese cruelly. She stated that
work should not be resumed unless the demands were accepted
and that should the strike last long, she could provide workers
with rice tickets, whereupon she produced four rice tickets,
without stating the place where these tickets were obtained.
She gave me one ticket and I signed a cross on a pad produced
by her. I then returned home and I did not know when Siao
Ningpo left the alleyway.

As a rule, when I went to the market in the morning, I saw
Siao Ning Po standing in the cotton shop, Yangtsepoo Road,
and when asked, she replied that she was staying at this
address in the room above the kitchen.

Two days later I went above to the cotton shop and saw
her in her room. I asked her when work could be resumed and
she advised me to wait until a settlement of the dispute was
effected. I remained there about 5 minutes and then left.

On the following day, when I was at neighbour's home,
Keng Di came to see me and giving me ten rice tickets told
me to distribute them to poor workers. I accepted, and
distributed to the following:-

1. Zung Di Tas (陈弟仔) ex-mill workers of the Dong Shing
Cotton Mill, staying in Zung Yuan
Li alleyway Yipoo Road.
2 tickets.

2. Sisu Wan Tas (小凤仔), ex-worker of the Fine Yarn Room
of the Dong Shing Mill, relative of
Zung Di Tas.
2 tickets.

第二天，当我在弄堂里和两个邻居织毛衣时，萧宁波出现在弄堂里，开始谈论劳工局势，说所有中国人都应该团结起来，日本人总是残酷对待中国人。她说除非要求得到接受，否则不应复工，如果罢工持续时间长，她可以为工人提供米票，随即她拿出四张米票，未说明这些米票的来源。她给了我一张票，我在她拿出的本子上画了一个十字。然后我回家，不知道萧宁波何时离开弄堂。

通常，当我早上去市场时，我看到萧宁波站在杨树浦路的棉花店里，询问时，她回答说住在这个地址厨房上面的房间里。

两天后，我去棉花店楼上，在她的房间里看到了她。我问她何时可以复工，她建议我等到纠纷解决为止。我在那里待了大约5分钟，然后离开。

第二天，当我在邻居家时，康弟来看我，给我十张米票，让我分发给贫困工人。我接受了，并分发给以下人员：-

1. 陈弟仔，前东兴纱厂工人，住在杨树浦路莊源里弄堂。
2张票。

2. 小凤仔，前东兴纱厂细纱间工人，陈弟仔的亲戚。
2张票。

I kept one for myself and in the evening of the same day when
I met Keng Di on Yangtzepoo Road, returned her the remaining
five tickets.

The following day an old woman named Wong Ah San, staying
at a country house, 7th Wei Fang, off Yangtzepoo Road,
whom I knew in the market came to my house and told me
that Siao Ning Po wanted me to go to her house the following
day in the afternoon and take two more girls along.

Consequently at 4 p.m. the following day I took with me two
girls named Siao Mih Chang (小蜜香) staying in House No. 3,
4th Lane, Hrc Ching Tsang; and Chao Kwei Ying (赵桂英),
staying at No. 99 Pang Zung Li, and proceeded to the cotton
shop in Siao Nitze's road, I saw Siao Ning Po and another
male Chinese, age about 27, 5'4" in height, small square face,
white complexion, dressed in blue pyjama. A few minutes
later, Keng Di came along, and then the male Chinese addressed
us, by stating that all should persist in the strike in order
to get an increase in wages and promising to supply the
strikers with rice tickets. He stated that he came from
Shanghai and asked that should anybody desire to attend meetings
he could go with him. He did not give the name of any
organisation or address. In the meantime, he took from the
drawer of the dressing table near the window a pad of black
ruled blank forms and without mentioning any purpose, wrote
down the names of persons present, one on each page. No
discussion took place and I subsequently left with my two
colleagues. The above is my true statement.
Signed Wong Siao Mei and thumb
printed.

我留了一张给自己，并在当天晚上于杨树浦路遇到耿迪（音译）时，将剩下的五张票还给了她。

次日，一位名叫黄阿三的老妇人来到我家。她住在杨树浦路旁卫坊七号的一间乡间房屋内，是我在菜场认识的。她告诉我，小宁波（音译）希望我次日下午去她家，并再带两名女孩同去。

因此，次日下午4时，我带着两名女孩前往小尼子路（音译）的棉布店。这两名女孩分别是：小蜜香，住在赫清藏（音译）四弄三号；赵桂英，住在邦宗里（音译）99号。在那里，我见到了小宁波和另一名中国男子，年龄约27岁，身高5英尺4英寸，方脸，肤色白皙，身穿蓝色睡衣。几分钟后，耿迪也来了。随后，那名中国男子对我们讲话，声称为了争取加薪，所有人都必须坚持罢工，并承诺向罢工者提供米票。他称自己来自上海，并表示如果有人想参加会议，可以随他一同前往。他没有提及任何组织名称或地址。其间，他从窗边梳妆台的抽屉里拿出一本黑色横线空白表单簿，未说明任何目的，便在每一页上写下一名在场者的姓名。期间并未进行讨论，随后我与两位同事离开。以上是我的真实陈述。
签署人：黄小妹（音译），并按指印。

My name is Yang Siau Tsoong (楊孝忠) alias Ma Ts (麻子),
age 24, native of Kompo, s/unemployed, residing country house,
Hinching Road.
I was born in Kau Yeu (高郵), Kompo, and remained
there until I was 11 years old, but did not attend any school.
On arrival in Shanghai I lived at a country house on Pingliang
Road with my father, mother and sister. My father being
a mason's labourer. At this time I took up studies at a
small primary school in Ten Teh Li alleyway, Tseu Na Sa Road,
the principal of which was one named Tsang (張). I
remained at this school for two and half years, after which I
commenced working as a shoemaker at Tsu Ng Du (九畝地),
Wantao. I remained in this job for about one year, but owing
to financial difficulties at home, I was forced to return home.
At age of 14 I commenced working in Shanghai No. 3 Cotton Mill,
weaving department, where I remained for 2 years. During my
working therein I had an accident, which resulted in me staying
in the St. Lukes Hospital for 3 months, during which time I
received half pay from the company. For a further period of
4 months I did not work, but remained at home. I then commenced
working as a casual labourer wherever I could find work. This
occupation I followed until I attained the age of 21 years. I
then started working in the Sung Sing No. 6 Mill, Weaving
Department where I remained until December 1935. Since that
time I have been unemployed. I was dismissed from Sung Sing
Mill through neglect of work.
On the 14/11/36 whilst in my home a number of my friends

我叫杨孝忠，别名麻子，24岁，籍贯高邮，无业，居住在兴昌路（音译）的一间乡间房屋内。
我出生于高邮，并在那里生活到11岁，但未上过学。抵达上海后，我与父母及妹妹住在平凉路的一间乡间房屋内。我的父亲是一名泥瓦匠小工。当时，我在滋纳萨路（音译）腾德里巷的一所小型小学读书，校长姓张。我在那所学校读了两年半，之后开始在万陶九亩地（Tsu Ng Du）做鞋匠。我从事这份工作约一年，但因家庭经济困难，被迫回家。14岁时，我开始在上海第三棉纺厂织布部工作，在那里工作了2年。在工作期间，我遭遇了一次事故，导致我在圣卢克医院（St. Lukes Hospital）住了3个月，在此期间公司向我发放半薪。此后4个月我没有工作，待在家里。随后，我开始 wherever 能找到工作就做临时工。我从事这一职业直到21岁。之后，我开始在松星六厂（Sung Sing No. 6 Mill）织布部工作，一直工作到1935年12月。自那时起，我一直失业。我因工作疏忽被松星厂解雇。

The following is the statement of Sung Zai Chang ( 沈增祥 ).

My name is Sung Zai Chang alias Siou Tsau Ts, age 22,
native of Yangchow, employed as a coiler in the spinning
department of Dah Kung Cotton Mill, Yangtzepoo Road, and residing
at an unnamed street, at, Yangtzepoo and Mingwa Roads corner.
I was born in Yangchow, and lived there until I was 14
years old. I first attended a small private school in
Yangchow, the principal of which was named Yang, and later
when I came to Shanghai at the age of 14 years, I attended the
Yangchow Guild Primary School on Hardoon Road for six years,
then under the headmastership of one named Tang. On leaving
this school, I attended Tse Zing On ( 静安 ) Primary School
next to the post office at B'well for one year. My teacher
at this school was named Jou Zung Ming ( 周仲明 ). During
the time that I attended these two schools, I lived at Wing
Ong Fang ( 永芳浜 ), 5000 Weil Road, along with my father,
who was employed as a chauffeur with one named Vong, a Chinese
lawyer. Owing to my father becoming old and being unable to
work, I decided to get a job, and came to live with my aunt in
my present address, where I have lived for about 1 year. On
coming to Yangtzepoo district, I at first obtained a job
with the Lei Tung ( 通 ) Cotton Mill, but after four days
I left to take up my present job in the Dah Kung Cotton Mill.
On joining this firm, I told lies, in respect to my previous
experience, stating that I had been employed in the Shanghai
Cotton Mills for 3 years. If I had not said so I could not
have obtained a position, as they only wanted men with experien-
ce.

我叫沈增祥，别名小曹子（音译），22岁，籍贯扬州，受雇于杨树浦路大康纱厂纺纱部担任卷绕工，居住在杨树浦路与明华路转角处一条无名街道上。
我出生于扬州，并在那里生活到14岁。我最初在扬州的一所小型私塾读书，校长姓杨。后来，我在14岁时来到上海，在哈同路（Hardoon Road）的扬州公会小学读了六年书，当时的校长姓唐。离开该校后，我在百老汇邮局旁边的静安小学读了一年书。我在那所学校的老师叫周仲明。在我就读这两所学校期间，我与父亲住在威妥玛路（Weil Road）5000号永芳浜。我的父亲受雇于一位姓王的华人律师，担任司机。由于父亲年迈无法工作，我决定找份工作，便搬来与我阿姨同住于现址，至今已居住约1年。来到杨树浦区后，我最初在通泰纱厂（Lei Tung Cotton Mill）找到一份工作，但四天后我离职，转而从事目前在大康纱厂的工作。在加入该公司时，我在以往经历方面撒了谎，声称我曾在上海各棉纺厂工作过3年。如果我不这么说，我就无法获得职位，因为他们只想要有经验的人。

During the recent strike in Japanese mills in the Yangtze-poo district, I continued to work between the 10th and 17th, of November 1936, although on many occasions during that time I was threatened with assault by workers of the Dong Shing and Shanghai Cotton Mills whilst walking on the roadway. On the night of the 16/11/36, after having partaken of my evening meal, I proceeded to Yangtzepoo Road for purpose of buying electric batteries for my torch, I having received my pay that day, and when near Liao Ning Road I met the accused Ma Ts ( 麻子 ) who I became acquainted with about one month previous, through the introduction of my co-worker Chen Keng Hao ( 陈根号 ) who lives in a straw hut on Sincing Road. On this occasion Ma Ts asked me if the strike had been settled and when I replied in the affirmative, he stated that as Dong Shing and Shanghai Cotton Mills had not yet settled their strike it was for us at Dah Kong help them. He then handed me five application forms and requested that I circulate them amongst the workers in the mill. He explained to me that anyone who signed such forms and struck work, would be supplied with rice coupons during the strike period. I took the forms from him without asking who was behind the strike movement and who was going to pay for the rice coupons. I knew I was wrong in doing so, inasmuch that the strike at Dah Kong had been settled and the wages increased. The following morning (17th) prior to going to work I took these application forms and along with a fountain pen put them inside my electric torch, for purpose of taking them to the mill. On arrival there, I

My name Voong Tsu Sz, age 65, Kompo, residing at
55/229, Tseu Ka Ba Road. My husband is farming in my
native place. My granddaughter named Soo-seng ( 素貞 )
and another girl named Yuen In ( 元英 ) whose mother left
for Kompo about a month ago, are living with me and they
are employees at Shanghai No. 7 Cotton Mill.

In the afternoon, one day, (I could not remember the
date) one male Chinese whose surname known to me as Yang
residing in the neighbourhood came to my house when he asked
me whether or not our girls were working in the mill. I
replied him in the affirmative. He told me that some people
outside would beat up the mill girls and if the names of our
girls are written on a paper, they would be beaten up. At
that time, some children were playing outside the door and
when they heard this, they shouted the names of our two
girls to this man who wrote same on a piece of paper and
walked away. This man wears blue jacket and pants and I
understand he is at present detained in the police station.

Signed and thumb printed.

我叫 Voong Tsu Sz，65岁，高邮人，居住在曹家渡路（Tseu Ka Ba Road）55/229号。我的丈夫在我的家乡务农。我的孙女素贞（Soo-seng）和另一个名叫元英（Yuen In）的女孩与我同住，元英的母亲大约一个月前去了高邮。她们都是上海第七棉纺厂的雇员。

有一天下午（我不记得具体日期了），一个姓杨的中国男子来到我家，他就住在附近。他问我家的女孩是否在工厂做工。我给予了肯定答复。他告诉我，外面有些人会殴打工厂的女工，如果把我们要女孩的名字写在一张纸上，她们就不会被打。当时，有些孩子在门外玩耍，听到这话，他们向这个人喊出了我们要两个女孩的名字，这个人把名字写在一张纸上后就走了。这个人穿着蓝色的夹克和裤子，据我所知，他目前被拘留在警察局。

签名并按指印。

我叫李周氏（Li Zau Sz），30岁，高邮人，居住在曹家渡路（Tseu Ka Ba Road）55/229号。我的丈夫李桂生（Li Kwei Sing）在江边发电站工作，已在那里服务了14年。我的小姑子李素珍（Li Soo Tseng）在上海第三棉纺厂工作。在某天下午（我不记得具体日期了），一名身份不明的中国男子来到我家，问我：“你家的女孩现在在工厂做工吗？”我给予了肯定答复。那人随后告诉我，外面有人会殴打女工，如果把他携带的一张纸上写上我们要家女孩的名字，就没有人会打她。听到这话，我告诉了他小姑子的名字。那人把名字写在一张纸上后就走了。

My name is Wong Ai Pau, native of Ningpo, age 20, residing with my sister named Wong Miau Ying (王妙英) at 1893 Y'poo Road. I was born in Ningpo, I have never attended school. I came to Shanghai when I was 6 years of age, and was living with my father at 1893 Y'poo Road. At that time my father was employed as a boy on board a river boat. About 7 years ago, my father returned to his native place in Ningpo. During the 11th moon last year, I was married to one named Zeu Sung Jiang (单生祥) but was divorced one month later. At the age of nine, I obtained a position as an apprentice in the San Sing Cotton Mill, Y'poo Road, where I worked for about 4 years. I then returned to Ningpo, where I stayed for approximately two months, and then returned to Shanghai. I was then successful in obtaining a post in the Spinning Dept., of the Shanghai No. 5 Cotton Mill, which post I held for a period of 4 years.

Owing to the death of my mother I returned to Ningpo, where I stayed for about one year. On returning to Shanghai, I became married to Zeu Sung Jiang. My marriage however was not a success, resulting in obtaining a divorce a month later. On my own initiative I secured a position in the Spinning Dept., of the Dong Shing Cotton Mill, Y'poo Road, where I was employed until the recent strike on 8/11/36. I did not want to go on strike, but was forced to do so by the other employees of the Dong Shing Mill with a view of enforcing the management to give us an increase in wages.

Between 8/11/36 and 14/11/36, I stayed at home, the only occasion I left home was for the purpose of buying vegetables at

以下为王爱宝（Wong Ai Pau）之陈述，
该人籍贯为宁波，由本人 Leys 警佐（D.S.）
于1936年11月23日在杨树浦警局（Y'poo Stn.）录取，并由沈翻译员（Interpreter Shen）翻译。

我叫王爱宝，宁波人，现年20岁，与我的姐姐王妙英（Wong Miau Ying）同住在杨树浦路1893号。我出生在宁波，从未上过学。我6岁时来到上海，与父亲同住在杨树浦路1893号。当时，我父亲在一艘内河轮船上做侍者。大约7年前，我父亲回到了他的家乡宁波。去年农历十一月，我与单生祥（Zeu Sung Jiang）结婚，但一个月后离婚。9岁时，我在杨树浦路的三星棉纺厂（San Sing Cotton Mill）获得了一个学徒职位，在那里工作了大约4年。随后我回到宁波，呆了大约两个月，然后又回到上海。之后，我成功在上海第五棉纺厂纺纱部获得了一个职位，该职位我担任了4年。

由于母亲去世，我回到宁波，在那里呆了大约一年。回到上海后，我与单生祥结婚。然而，我的婚姻并不成功，导致一个月后离婚。我主动在东兴纱厂（Dong Shing Cotton Mill，位于杨树浦路）纺纱部谋得一个职位，一直工作到最近1936年11月8日的罢工。我不想罢工，但被东兴纱厂的其他员工强迫这样做，目的是迫使管理层给我们增加工资。

在1936年11月8日至11月14日期间，我呆在家里，唯一外出的情况是为了买蔬菜，地点在

Sungpan Road Market. During this period none of the strikers visited my home. I did not meet any strikers during my visits at Sungpan Road Market.

At 5.30 p.m. 14/11/36, I left home with the intention of proceeding to the Dong Shing Cotton Mill, to ascertain whether or not the strike had been settled, and whilst passing Ye Zung Li, off Y'poo Road, I observed a crowd of strikers, one of which was a female named Ling Keng Di (林根弟) an employee of Dong Shing Cotton Mill, on permanent day shift. This female was addressing the strikers, advising them to persist in the strike, otherwise they would be beaten. This female went on to state, that if they continued the strike, they would be supplied with rice tickets. Ling Keng Di wrote the names of those present on a piece of paper and left that location. I then returned home. I did not receive any rice tickets from Ling Keng De nor did I distribute these tickets to other strikers.

I do not know why I should be implicated by Wong Siau Mei, as having taken an active part in this strike.

The above is my true statement.

Signed and thumb printed.
Wong Ai Pau.

嵩山路（Sungpan Road）市场。在此期间，没有任何罢工者来过我家。我在去嵩山路市场时也没有遇到任何罢工者。

1936年11月14日下午5点30分，我离开家，打算去东兴纱厂，以查明罢工是否已经解决。当经过杨树浦路附近的叶宗里（Ye Zung Li，音译）时，我看到一群罢工者，其中有一位名叫林根弟（Ling Keng Di）的女性，她是东兴纱厂的雇员，上常日班。这名女性正在对罢工者讲话，劝告他们坚持罢工，否则他们会挨打。这名女性接着说，如果他们继续罢工，他们将获得米票。林根弟把在场人员的名字写在一张纸上，然后离开了那个地方。随后我回了家。我没有从林根弟那里收到任何米票，也没有向其他罢工者分发这些米票。

我不知道为什么王小妹（Wong Siau Mei）会牵连我，说我积极参与了这次罢工。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名并按指印。

Made by... D.S.I.Burton. Forwarded by O : A Perkins Insp.

Sir,

At 3 P.M. on the 18.11.36., a male Chinese member of the Zung
Yee (□ □) Salvation Association bought from the Zang Fah (長發)
Rice Shop, No.401 Robison Road, O.O.L. rice to the value of $100.00
and on buying this rice, made arrangements with the shop owner that
he would distribute rice tickets valued 50 cents, which when present-
ed at the shop were to be torn in half, one portion to be retained
by the shop keeper and the other portion returned to the person
presenting the ticket.

On the afternoon of 19.11.36., these 200 rice tickets were
distributed to N.W.K. temporary workers who are on strike and not
in possession of mill attendance books. Up to the present 30 of these
50 cents tickets have been presented at the shop. Portion sample
of one of the tickets attached.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,

D.S.I.

Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [Signature] Inspt. O. i/c

Sir,
I beg to report, that at 6.50 a.m. 15/11/36, U.P.C. 90
on duty at the Tai Foong ( 高丰 ) Rice shop, situated at
2035 Yangtzepoo Road for purpose of intercepting persons
attempting to cash rice coupons, brought to the station a
female child named Koo Sing San ( 顾新三 ), age 14, native
of Nomo, residing 42 Tin Zang Li ( 依仁里 ), Yangtzepoo Road
who at 6.30 a.m. had entered the above shop and tendered two
coupons for rice.
This child on being questioned as to the origin of these
coupons stated at 4.30 p.m. 17/11/36, two Chinese females
undoubtedly of the student class visited her home and after
enquiring as to how many girls employed in Japanese mills
lived therein, handed her the two coupons, along with instruc-
tions that she was to give the two coupons to the four girls,
all employees of Dong Ching Mill, and inform them that they
were to cease work, failing which they would be severely dealt
with.
Description of the two females is as follows:-
(1) Age about 18, height 4'9", medium build, round face, fair
complexion, bobbed hair, wearing blue long gown carrying
a woolen jumper over her arm and under which she carried
the rice coupons. Spoke Shanghai dialect.
(2) Age about 20, height 5'1", long thin face, dark complexion,
long hair to the shoulders, with straight cut fringe over
the forehead, wearing black long gown, carrying a brown
woolen jumper, spoke Shanghai dialect.
This child was allowed to take the rice, and the two coupons
were later handed to the Police by the shop-master.

Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [Signature] Inspt. C. i/c

Sir,

I beg to report that throughout the day of 17/11/36, the following unconfirmed information was obtained by detectives working on the local Japanese mill situation.

At 2 p.m. on the 10/11/36, a meeting composed of about 20 persons, amongst whom were teachers of the Lin Ching Primary School, was held in the Yih Tuh Li ( 昭德里 ) alleyway, Yangtszepoo Road.

It was during the course of this meeting that the introduction of rice coupons was made, and the instructions were to the effect, that these tickets were to be used as a means of propaganda i.e. on some being given to a mill worker, her work book, should be taken from her, as an assurance that she would not return to work. Whether the later part of this information, is true or otherwise, could not be substantiated, however with the arrest of one of the distributors by Yangtszepoo on the 17/11/36, it is hoped to clear this part up. (See Misc. No. 284/36 Y).

On the evening of the 13/11/36, a number of students of the Lin Ching Primary School, held a meeting in an unknown straw hut at the rear of Zung Zung Li ( 顺成里 ), Tseu Ka Ba Road. At this meeting the man Ts An Hyi ( 朱阿二 ) suspected ringleader presided.

At 2 p.m. on the 14/11/36, another meeting similar to the other two was held in the Yih Tuh Li Alleyway.

Between 10 and 11 a.m. 16/11/36, twenty ex-employees of the Sai Yeu ( 三友 ) Towel Factory, held a meeting on a piece of waste ground at the rear of Ying Ziang Kong Village, and at this meeting it was decided that they offer their services to the strike movement in Yangtszepoo district.

先生，

谨此报告，在1936年11月17日全天，负责调查当地日商纱厂局势的侦探获得了以下未经证实的情报。

1936年11月10日下午2时，在杨树浦路昭德里（Yih Tuh Li）弄堂内举行了一次会议，与会者约20人，其中包括林青小学（Lin Ching Primary School）的教师。

正是在这次会议期间，提出了发放米票的事宜，指示大意是，这些票证将被用作宣传手段，即当其中一些票证发给一名女工时，应没收其工作证，以此作为她不再复工的保证。至于该情报的后半部分是否属实，目前尚无法证实，但随着杨树浦警方于1936年11月17日逮捕了一名分发者，希望能澄清这一部分情况。（参见杂项档案第284/36 Y号）。

1936年11月13日晚，林青小学的一些学生在周家嘴路（Tseu Ka Ba Road）顺成里（Zung Zung Li）后方的一间不知名的草棚内举行会议。在这次会议上，嫌疑主谋朱阿二（Ts An Hyi）主持了会议。

1936年11月14日下午2时，在昭德里弄堂内举行了另一次与前两次类似的会议。

1936年11月16日上午10时至11时之间，三友（Sai Yeu）毛巾厂的二十名前雇员在引翔港村（Ying Ziang Kong Village）后方的一块空地上举行会议，会上决定他们将为杨树浦地区的罢工运动提供服务。

the strike to take place on the 17/11/36, at the Naigai-wata-
Gaisha No. 2 Mill in the western district.

1. 在各日商纱厂的所有部门建立分部小组。
2. 成立宣传组。

参加会议的大多数人是安徽籍人士，据称在会议期间，朱阿二发表演讲，大意是救国会支持在所有日商纱厂发动总罢工的行动，罢工将于1936年11月17日在西区的中棉二厂（Naigai-wata-Gaisha No. 2 Mill）开始。

C.D.C. 108 received information to the effect that strong efforts
were being made by the National Salvation Association, to
intimidate the workers of the Shanghai Nos. 2 and 8 Mill and Dong
Shing Mill to remain on strike, and that in every probability these
mill workers would as a result of such intimidation, cease work
after all had received their wages on the 16-17 and 18th November
1936. Further information was to the effect that the mode of
intimidate adopted by the aforesaid association, was in the form
of supplying the workers with rice, purchasing coupons, these
having already been bought by members of the association at
various rice shops in the Yangtszepoo District.

In order to test the strength of this information, a visit
was paid to all rice hong's in this district, during the morning
of the 16/11/36, with the following results.

(1st) Lau Wai Foong (老茂丰) Rice Hong, situated at 1537 Y'poo
Road.

At 8 a.m. 14/11/36, a Chinese female, age about 30, height
5'2", medium build, long square face, dark complexion, hair
combed straight back, and tied in a bun at the nape of her neck,
wearing black cootton short jacket and pants, appearance of mill
worker, speaking Shanghai and Kompo dialects, entered above shop,
and requested a shop-assistant to supply her with $30.00 worth of
50¢ Rice Coupons. This assistant questioned the female as to
who she was and why she wanted these coupons, and in reply she
stated that she was purchasing them on behalf of a society to
supply to the poor in Yangtszepoo District. The shop-assistant
not being satisfied with her answer refered the matter to his

Translation of a poster found on the wall of
Zung Zung Li alleyway Tsu Ka Ba Road, 16/11/36.
--------
Dear fellow workers:-
Let us all go to the City Government to request assistance
to-day. We all should unite with each other if our Japanese
employers will not comply with our demands. We must reach our
object first and then resume work. We must not turn up to work
to-day as part of our workers has been bribed by the Japanese.
Those who have been bribed are running dogs and we should unite
together to beat up these running dogs. Whoever goes to work
today is a running dog and we are going to beat him up. We
hope that all the workers will fight to the end in order to
reach a glorious victory.

Declared by all the workers.

--------
亲爱的工友们：
让我们今天都去市政府请求援助。如果我们的日本雇主不答应我们的要求，我们都应该团结起来。我们必须先达到目的，然后再复工。我们今天不能去上班，因为我们的一部分工人已被日本人收买。那些被收买的人是走狗，我们应该联合起来痛打这些走狗。今天谁去上班谁就是走狗，我们要揍他。我们希望所有工人为取得光荣的胜利而奋斗到底。

全体工人宣告。

the undersigned, who was then accompanied by D.S.I. Sung Ah Foh,
J.D.S. 42 and C.D.C. 108, was drawn to a female who had just
been addressing a number of workers, and who was identified by
S.I. Turner, then present, as one of the ringleaders in the
party of strikers who came to Yangtsepoo Station on the night
of 11/11/36, demanding the release of one named Sze Yee Ziang
(施维祥) (see Misc. Report No. 266/36 and F.I.R. 622/36 Y).
On being informed of the latter incident, the undersigned
approached the female, requested her to accompany him to the
station for enquiries. She at first refused, stating that she
was an employee of the Dah Kong Mill, and that she had come
there in order to ascertain whether or not the night shift was
going on duty. In order to corroborate this statement she was
taken to the offices of the Dah Kong Mill, and as a result the
following particulars were ascertained:-
Name Waung Siau Mei (王小妹) age 20, employed in the
spinning department, Number 6048, record of character states,
"Good worker but frequently quarrels and fights with other
females." This female when questioned as to where she lived,
gave her address as 18 Yeu Yih Foong (元益坊), Yangtsepoo
Road. A visit to this address was made, but nothing of an
incriminating nature was found.
On being brought to station this female was for a long time
very reluctant to answer any questions put to her, however after
she had been identified by S.I. Taplin, S.I. Turner, F.S. 90

谨报告如下：1936年11月11日下午6时30分，当在裕丰和大康纱厂之间的杨树浦路上巡逻，搜寻煽动者时，署名警官（当时由副督察宋阿福 D.S.I. Sung Ah Foh、高级警士 J.D.S. 42 和刑事侦缉处探员 C.D.C. 108 陪同）注意到一名女子刚刚向一群工人发表讲话，当时在场的警佐特纳 S.I. Turner 指认她是1936年11月11日晚来到杨树浦警署、要求释放一名叫施维祥 Sze Yee Ziang 的罢工者团伙中的头目之一（参见杂项报告第266/36号和首次情报报告 F.I.R. 622/36 Y）。
得知上述情况后，署名警官走近该女子，要求她随同前往警署接受问询。她起初拒绝，声称自己是大康纱厂的雇员，去那里是为了确认夜班是否正在上岗。为了证实这一说法，她被带到大康纱厂办事处，结果查明了以下详情：
姓名：王小妹 Waung Siau Mei，年龄20岁，受雇于纺纱部，编号6048，品行记录显示：“工作良好，但经常与其他女性争吵打架。”当被问及居住地时，该女子给出的地址是杨树浦路元益坊18号。对该地址进行了走访，但未发现任何具有指控性质的物品。
将该女子带到警署后，她在很长一段时间内非常不愿回答向她提出的任何问题，然而，在警佐塔普林 S.I. Taplin、警佐特纳 S.I. Turner、高级警士 F.S. 90 指认她之后

February 22, 1937.    Morning Translation

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated February 21 and other local newspapers :-

THE TROUBLE AT THE TOYODA COTTON MILLS

As a result of mediation by the officials of the local Tangpu and Government organs, the night shift of the old and new Toyoda Cotton Mills, No. 200 Jessfield Road, resumed work at 5.30 p.m. February 20 and worked until 10 a.m. February 21. The 13 workers who were arrested have been handed over to the Police Bureau for detention. Although it was at first intended to release the arrested workers on bail after the strikers had resumed work, they have now been arraigned in Court despite the fact that the strikers have resumed operations.

For this reason, the entire body of the workers have become angry and have therefore appointed representatives to make further appeals to the local Tangpu and other Government organs. It is learned that the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang Headquarters have detailed an official to call on Mr. O.K. Yui, Chief Secretary of the Shanghai City Government, with a request that the Police Bureau be immediately notified to release the arrested workers on bail so as to avoid further dispute.

After the clash between the workers of the Toyoda Cotton Mills and the Police, the "Welfare Association of Employees of Japanese Cotton Mills in the Western District of Shanghai" was searched and sealed by the Zao Ka Doo Branch Police Bureau, and several policemen were detailed to guard the premises.

According to information secured by the Ta Kung News Agency, this Association was established with the permission of the local Tangpu and other Government organs. Despite the illegal action of the Police, the Association is still functioning and is appealing to the Tangpu and other Government organs for assistance.

When interviewed by a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency, a responsible official of the Staff Department of the new Toyoda Cotton Mills stated that the management of the factory regrets the trouble between the workers and the Police, but as the strikers had now resumed work, the dispute was regarded as having come to an end.

Mr. Funatsu, Chairman of the Japanese Cotton Mills Owners' Association has made an inspection of the Toyoda Cotton Mill. He will make a report on his inspection to the meeting of the Standing Committee of the Association on Wednesday next.

Sun Hwo Wan Pao dated February 21 (Comment) :-

Shih Foh Ling Blamed for Mill Trouble

On February 20 a serious disturbance took place among the workers of the Toyoda Cotton Mill owing to a representative of the workers having been injured by desperadoes who had been bribed by Shih Foh Ling (施福林), a member of the staff of the mill, to attack him.

According to information secured by our reporter, Shih Foh Ling should be held responsible for the trouble. The authorities should make an investigation and deal with Shih, who is a traitor.

2月21日《华美晚报》及其他本地报纸：

丰田纱厂纠纷

经当地党部及政府机关官员调解，位于极司菲尔路200号的丰田新旧纱厂夜班工人于2月20日下午5时30分复工，工作至2月21日上午10时。被捕的13名工人已移交警察局拘留。虽然起初打算在罢工者复工后保释被捕工人，尽管罢工者已恢复生产，但他们现在仍被起诉至法院。

因此，全体工人大为愤怒，遂推选代表向当地党部及其他政府机关进一步请愿。据悉，国民党上海市特别市党部已指派一名官员拜访上海市政府秘书长余井塘先生，请求立即通知警察局保释被捕工人，以避免进一步争端。

丰田纱厂工人与警察发生冲突后，“上海西区日商纱厂职工福利会”被造甲杜分局警察局搜查并查封，并派遣数名警察看守该处。

据大公通讯社获得的消息，该协会是经当地党部及其他政府机关许可成立的。尽管警方采取非法行动，该协会仍在运作，并向党部及其他政府机关求助。

大公通讯社记者采访丰田新纱厂庶务科一位负责人时，该负责人表示，厂方对工人与警察之间的纠纷表示遗憾，但由于罢工者现已复工，争议被视为已经结束。

日本棉纺业同业公会会长船津先生视察了丰田纱厂。他将在下周三的公会常务委员会会议上汇报视察情况。

2月21日《申报》（评论）：

施福林被指应对纱厂纠纷负责

2月20日，丰田纱厂工人发生严重骚乱，起因是一名工人代表遭到暴徒袭击受伤，而这些暴徒是受该厂职员施福林贿赂指使的。

据本报记者获得的消息，施福林应对此次纠纷负责。当局应进行调查并处置这名汉奸施氏。

MAINICHI(20-2-37)

JAPAN AND BRITAIN'S ARMAMENT PROGRAMME

The Mainichi publishes the
following leading article:-
On February 18 the British
House of Commons passed a resolution authorizing the
government to issue national defence bonds to the amount
of £400,000,000 with which the British Government can
strengthen the air force and navy in five years. It
must not be overlooked that Great Britain also intends
to make an advance towards the Pacific. The construction
of the naval base at Singapore, the construction of an
aerodrome at Penang and the military construction work
at Kowloon show Great Britain's plans in the East Asia.
It is reported that some sort of understanding has been
reached between Great Britain and China regarding Hainan
Island. Great Britain will strengthen her fleet in China
waters. This measure and the American naval rearmament
constitute a danger to the peace of the Pacific.
Japan's national defence measures
are based on a non-aggression and non-encroachment policy.
For this reason, Japan does not care how far the United
States and Great Britain will expand their fighting forces.
We have to change our views regarding Great Britain because
of late she has been continuously ignoring Japan, the
stabilizing Power in East Asia. China is a good market
for British capital, therefore, she is endeavouring to
avoid friction with Japan. Sino-Japanese relations are
bound to improve for the present disputes between the
two countries only are temporary. It would be a mistake
on the part of Great Britain should she attempt to estrange
China from Japan.

KOREAN ABSCONDER ARRESTED BY JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

《每日新闻》（1937年2月20日）

日本与英国的军备计划

《每日新闻》刊登以下社论：
2月18日，英国下议院通过一项决议，授权政府发行4亿英镑的国防债券，英国政府可借此在五年内加强空军和海军力量。不可忽视的是，英国还意图向太平洋推进。新加坡海军基地的建设、槟城机场的建设以及九龙的军事建设工程，显示了英国在东亚的计划。据报道，英国与中国就海南岛问题达成了某种谅解。英国将加强其在中国水域的舰队。这一措施与美国的海军重整军备构成了对太平洋和平的威胁。
日本的国防措施基于不侵略和不扩张政策。因此，日本并不在意美国和英国将其战斗部队扩张到何种程度。由于英国近期持续忽视作为东亚稳定力量的日本，我们不得不改变对英国的看法。中国是英国资本的良好市场，因此英国正努力避免与日本发生摩擦。中日关系必将改善，因为两国目前的争端只是暂时的。如果英国试图离间中日关系，那将是错误的。

Morning Translation

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:

MILL WORKERS ATTACK CHINESE POLICE STATION

(孫肇泰), On the evening of February 18, Sung Chien Tai
a representative of the workers of the old Toyoda
Cotton Mill to the "Welfare Association of Employees of
Japanese Cotton Mills in the Western District of Shanghai,"
was attacked and wounded by certain desperadoes with knives.
The 3,000 workers of both the new and old Toyoda
cotton mills became indignant upon learning that the attack
was carried out by certain persons who had been paid $300
by Shih Foh Ling (施福林), an overseer of the mill, to
make the attack and that an interpreter named Shih Ching
Chung (時景春) had also taken part in the affair.
At 6 a.m. yesterday when the day shift began
their work and the night shift was leaving the mill, a strike
was declared. The strikers immediately rounded up the
overseer and the interpreter in question.
Upon learning of this, Colonel Tan Pao Shou
(譚葆壽), Chief of the Zao Ka Doo Branch Police Bureau,
and his men rescued the overseer and the interpreter and
took them to the Chung San Road Sub-Station.
About 2,000 strikers then went to the Zao Ka
Doo Branch Police Bureau to make an appeal, reaching there
at 6.30 a.m.. As the Colonel had not yet returned from
the Chung San Road Sub-Station, the strikers rushed into
the Branch Bureau, damaged the furniture, etc. and injured
two policemen with wooden bars. When the Colonel and
the overseer and the interpreter returned, the strikers
assaulted the three men. Colonel Tan Pao Shou was injured
in the head. Shih Foh Ling, the overseer, was dragged
by the strikers to the Welfare Association where he was
assaulted.
Colonel Tan Pao Shou was rushed to the Red Cross
Society Hospital for treatment. It is understood that his
injury is not serious. Shih Foh Ling is reported to
have incurred slight injuries while the interpreter Shih
Ching Chung made good his escape.
Upon receiving a report of the trouble, the
Headquarters of the Police Bureau despatched a large number
of policemen and two riot vans to Zao Ka Doo to quell the
mob and to persuade them to disperse. The strikers
adopted a strong attitude so the Police fired several shots
as a warning. Four workers were wounded or injured.
It was not until 9 a.m. that the strikers were completely
dispersed. Normal conditions were restored at the Branch
Bureau at about 10 a.m.
Cheu Hoong Nyi (周洪年) and 12 other workers
who were arrested were escorted to the Headquarters of the
Police Bureau while the wounded and injured workers were
sent to the Red Cross Society Hospital.
When the matter came to the notice of the Bureau
of Social Affairs, officials were detailed to make an
investigation. The local Tangpu did likewise.
Yesterday afternoon, the local Tangpu, the Bureau
of Social Affairs, the Police Bureau and the General Labour
Union held a meeting at which the following resolutions
were passed:-

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

纱厂工人袭击中国警察局

（孫肇泰），2月18日晚，孙肇泰作为旧丰田棉厂工人代表前往“上海西区日商纱厂职工福利会”，被几名暴徒持刀袭击致伤。新旧丰田棉厂的3000名工人得知此次袭击是由该厂监工施福林（Shih Foh Ling）出资300美元指使某些人实施，且一名名为时景春（Shih Ching Chung）的翻译也参与了此事后，群情激愤。
昨日清晨6点，当日班开始工作、夜班离开工厂时，宣布罢工。罢工者立即围住了上述监工和翻译。
闸北分局警察局局长谭葆寿（Tan Pao Shou）上校及其手下获悉此事后，救出了监工和翻译，并将他们带至中山路分驻所。
随后约2000名罢工者于上午6点30分抵达闸北分局请愿。由于谭上校尚未从中山路分驻所返回，罢工者冲入分局，损坏家具等物，并用木棍打伤两名警察。当谭上校与监工及翻译返回时，罢工者袭击了这三人。谭葆寿上校头部受伤。监工施福林被罢工者拖至福利会并遭到殴打。
谭葆寿上校被紧急送往红十字会医院救治。据悉其伤势不重。据报道，施福林受轻伤，而翻译时景春则成功逃脱。
警局总部接到骚乱报告后，派遣大量警员及两辆防暴车前往闸北平息暴乱并劝散人群。罢工者态度强硬，警方遂鸣枪示警。四名工人受伤。直至上午9点，罢工者才完全散去。上午10点左右，分局恢复正常秩序。
周洪年（Cheu Hoong Nyi）及其他12名被捕工人被押送至警局总部，受伤工人则被送往红十字会医院。
此事引起社会局注意后，该局指派官员进行调查。当地党部亦采取了同样行动。

The Livelihood Weekly ( 生活星期刊 ) in its issue of November 29
published the following letter written by "A Worker" -

THE STRUGGLE FOR A LIVING

On the night of November 17, a sanguinary
fight took place in the Toyoda Cotton Mill, a Japanese
concern, situated near the Chung San Bridge. I am not a
worker of the cotton mill. I stood about 50 feet away
from the mill and saw in the dark a crowd of people rushing
forward and another crowd retreating. An angry roar broke
out among the crowd that was pressing onward: "Don't be
afraid. Fight and kill these devils!"
My blood was also boiling. I went forward
in the wake of the angry crowd. Two tanks mounted with
machine guns went quickly by. The workers went forward
as if they were prepared to exchange their warm blood and
flesh for a living.
Angry shouts of "Fight, fight and kill the
man-eating devils!" finally scared the devils who retreated
to their underground rooms (which they had prepared specially
for use in time of war). I asked one of the workers the
cause of the trouble and he spoke as follows :-
"We work 14 hours a day. Our condition is
worse than that of cattle. We cannot even procure
sufficient food. We are unable to tolerate such hard
conditions any more, so we asked the mill management for
an increase of pay. The management caused us to be whipped
and increased our working hours. To-night, three of our
fellow workers were seen talking together by a Japanese
foreman and were immediately taken away. This infuriated
the entire body of workers who demanded the release of the
workers. Instead of accepting our demand, the management
arrested the workers who were appointed to make the demand
and tortured them. So we are risking our lives to demand
the release of the arrested workers and for an increase of
pay."

and that it was unfair to detain him at the Police Station.
The Judge then ordered the accused to be
held at the Detention House of the Court.

11月29日出版的《生活星期刊》刊登了一封署名为“一工人”的来信——

生存斗争

11月17日晚，在位于中山桥附近的日资企业丰田棉厂发生了一场血腥斗殴。我并非该棉厂工人。我站在距工厂约50英尺的地方，在黑暗中看到一群人向前冲，另一群人向后撤。向前涌动的人群中爆发出愤怒的吼声：“不要怕。打死这些鬼子！”
我的血液也在沸腾。我跟随愤怒的人群向前走去。两辆装有机关枪的坦克快速驶过。工人们向前推进，仿佛准备用他们的热血和肉体去换取生存。
“打，打死吃人的鬼子！”的愤怒喊声最终吓退了鬼子，他们退回到其地下房间（这是他们专门为战时准备使用的）。我向一名工人询问骚乱原因，他说道：-
“我们每天工作14小时。我们的处境比牛马还差。我们甚至无法获得足够的食物。我们再也无法忍受如此艰苦的条件，因此要求厂方增加工资。厂方却让人鞭打我们，并延长我们的工作时间。今晚，三名工友被一名日本领班看到在一起交谈，随即被带走。这激怒了全体工人，我们要求释放这些工人。厂方非但不接受我们的要求，反而逮捕了被指派提出要求的工人并对他们施以酷刑。因此，我们冒着生命危险要求释放被捕工人并增加工资。”

Further information indicates that Siao Jhen ( 小陳 )
presided over another 'cell' meeting held between 10.30 a.m.
and 1 p.m. December 28, 1936, by eight students (comprising
6 male and 2 female) of the Great China University in their
dormitory at No.57 Jhur Sun Road, Western Sharei. A new
nomenclature for these gatherings known as the "Jung Lih Tsu"
(Organization of United Strength) ( 群力斋 ) has been assumed.
The meeting discussed and passed the following resolutions:-
(1) That the Propaganda Section arrange to have anti-Chiang
Kai-shek slogans written with hard charcoal on various
thoroughfares in the vicinity of Jhun San Road.
(2) That approval be given to a newly elected comrade to
participate in all meetings (vide resolution passed on
December 21, 1936).
(3) That membership fees be collected in order to enable
the Propaganda Section to provide propaganda matter
during the year-end.
(4) That strongly determined comrades be detailed to various
streets in Sharei to remove and destroy handbills and/or
posters bearing on the welcome of General Chiang Kai-shek.
It has been definitely ascertained that Siao Chen,
who was mentioned in previous reports, has been transferred
to an unknown destination. The description and identity
of the aforementioned Siao Chen are given hereunder:-
Age 26/7, native of Ningpo, Chekiang, height 5'6",
long face, fresh complexion, usually wearing a dark grey
long gown and black leather shoes. His real name is
Chen Koh-tseng ( 陳國珍 ).

Cotton Mills, in the Tee Ming School (梯明小学), Lane 234, No.4 Mapai Road, at 8 p.m. December 5 and made the following report to the attendants:-

The following resolution was later discussed and passed:-

"That during the period commencing from December 5 to December 13, each active member (of their National Salvation Association) should recruit ten new members and submit a report on his individual work sometime next week. Some thirty Chinese claiming to be representatives
of workers of Japanese cotton mills in the Western District
held a meeting in the Tee Ming School (梯明中小学),
Lane 234, No.4 Mapai Road (Pootoo Road District) at 10.30
a.m. November 29, 1936. One named Siao Chen, who presided,
stated that the failure to obtain complete success during
the recent strike was entirely due to the traitorous
Mutual Aid Society, and urged the representatives to unite
together and form a labour union in order to prepare for
the second general strike for the purpose of enforcing
the following demands :-

1. That an increase of 20% in wages be granted.
2. That one hour be granted for tiffin.
3. That no workers be assaulted or dismissed.
4. That a bonus equivalent to four days' wages be granted
to all workers including those on leave.
5. That the three 8 hours shift system be adopted.
6. That Sundays be observed as holidays with full pay.
7. That all arrested workers be released and that all
dismissed workers be reinstated.

Subject WOO Shing Kao (吴星高) alleged labour agitator in the western
District.
Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by Chinese S.I.

With reference to the attached report from Lootoo
Road Station, discreet enquiries have been made regarding
one named Woo Shing Kao (吴星高), who was alleged to be
one of the ringleaders in the strike movement of the Japanese
cotton mill workers in the western District, and the instigator
of the riot staged by the workers of the Toyoda mill on
Jessfield and Chungshan Roads on November 17, 1936, and it
has been ascertained that there is one named Wu Shing Kao
(吴兴高), native of Kiangpeh, age about 25, who is an
ex-worker of the Dong Shing & Kung Dah Cotton mills, having
been unemployed for three years. During this period, he has
been self appointed representative of unemployed workers of
Japanese cotton mills, and since the Spring of this year, has
enlisted in the Labourers' National Salvation Association as
a messenger for the Eastern District.

This person is nothing but an opportunist, seizing
all ways and means to make money, even selling information
to any interested party. Although there is no evidence that
he has transferred his activities to the Western District,
there is every reason to believe that he might have parti-
cipated in some meetings in the Western District during the
last strike as a means to advertise his importance and attract
the attention of the Chinese Authorities, expecting that he
might be offered some employment later on, or remuneration
for information supplied.

He is reported to be living in a straw hut off Ningkuo
Road near Linching Road.

Sih Tse liang
D. I.

制作人 侦探员 施子良 转呈人 华籍巡长

参照来自卢图路（Lootoo Road）巡捕房的附呈报告，经对名为吴星高（吴星高）之人进行暗中查询，此人被指称为西区日本棉纺厂工人罢工运动的头目之一，以及1936年11月17日在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）和中山路丰田纱厂工人骚乱的煽动者。现已查明，有一人名叫吴兴高（Wu Shing Kao），江北人，年龄约25岁，系东盛与公大棉纺厂前工人，已失业三年。在此期间，他自封为日本棉纺厂失业工人代表，并自今年春季以来，加入劳工救国会，担任东区通讯员。

此人不过是个机会主义者，不择手段地谋取钱财，甚至向任何感兴趣的一方出售情报。虽然没有证据表明他已将活动转移至西区，但有充分理由相信，他可能在上次罢工期间参加了西区的一些会议，以此作为宣扬其重要性并引起中国当局注意的手段，期望日后能获得某种职位或因提供情报而获得报酬。

据报道，他住在宁国路附近临清路旁的一间草棚里。

Subject Meeting by Strikers of N.J.K. Mills O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I.Burton. Forwarded by A Perkins Insp.

Sir,
At 9:30 a.m. on the 19.11.36., male and female
strikers of the N.J.K. Mills, numbering 300, assembled outside
No.780 Chung Shan Road, Chapei, on a piece of vacant ground, and
and held a meeting.
They were addressed by three members of the National
Salvation Association namely:- Woo Shing Kau (吴星高), student,
Lee Liang (李良), School-teacher of the Garden Primary School, Garden
Road, Chapei, and Lee Tse Ling (李芝林), ex-clerk of the "B"
shift, N.J.K. No.2 Mill. The present strike situation was
discussed and the following resolutions passed:-
1. A wage increase of 20 per-cent be demanded.
2. No Sunday work.
3. That workers receive reward money.
4. Rules be drawn up regarding holidays.
5. That working hours be 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.
6. That 4 representatives from each mill be appointed
to appeal to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai
for assistance.
7. In the event of a non-favourable answer to the
resolutions, the strike to be continued.
8. No worker to be dismissed without just cause.
9. That all workers receive wages whilst on strike.
10. Temporary workers to be put on the permanent staff.
11. Dismissed workers to be reinstated.
12. That the workers' wages to be put on the same
basis as they were before January 26th, 1932.
13. All citizens of Shanghai to unite against the
Japanese Imperialists.

事由 老靶子路（O.O.L.）内山纱厂（N.J.K. Mills）罢工者会议

制作人 副侦探巡长 Burton. 转呈人 督察 Perkins.

先生，
1936年11月19日上午9时30分，内山纱厂男女罢工者共300人，聚集在闸北中山路780号外的一块空地上，并举行了会议。
三名救国会成员向他们发表了讲话，分别是：- 吴星高（Woo Shing Kau），学生；李良（Lee Liang），闸北花园路花园小学教师；以及李芝林（Lee Tse Ling），内山第二厂“B”班前职员。会议讨论了当前的罢工局势，并通过了以下决议：-
1. 要求增加工资20%。
2. 星期日不工作。
3. 工人应获得奖励金。
4. 制定有关假期的规则。
5. 工作时间为上午6时至下午6时。
6. 每厂指派4名代表向上海特别市政府请求援助。
7. 如果对上述决议得不到有利的答复，则继续罢工。
8. 无正当理由不得解雇任何工人。
9. 罢工期间所有工人照发工资。
10. 临时工转为正式员工。
11. 复职被解雇的工人。
12. 工人工资恢复至1932年1月26日之前的水平。
13. 上海全体市民联合起来反对日本帝国主义者。

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by (Signature)

At 7 a.m. November 25, nine Chinese claiming to be representatives of workers of the N.W.K. Nos. 1 and 2 mills and two Chinese named Siao Li ( 小 李 ) and Siao Zung ( 小 陳 ), claiming to be representatives of the Anti-Japanese National Salvation Association rented rooms Nos.235, 237 and 238 in the Great Shanghai hotel, 423 Tientsin Road, under the names of Chu Tai ( 朱 沂 ), Kiangsu, and Fang Chueh-an ( 方 覺 庵 ), Ningpo, for the purpose of welcoming workers who would be released from prison on the expiration of their sentences. At 2 p.m. thirty-one workers of whom 25 belonged to the N.W.K. No.1 mill and 6 to the N.W.K. No.2 mill, who claimed to have just been released from prison, arrived at the hotel, and a meeting to welcome them was held in Room No.237. Siao Li presided and stated that the spirit of the arrested workers in sacrificing their comfort for the benefit of all was praiseworthy and that all workers should follow their example. Before concluding his speech, he instructed the attendance to assemble at 7 a.m. November 27 at Chow Ka Jao ( 周 家 橋 ) near Chung San Road, for the purpose of proceeding to the Shanghai City Government and appealing for the release of the leaders of the National Salvation Movement who had been recently arrested by the Chinese Authorities. The attendance was also urged to bring as many workers as possible to participate in the delegation.

At the conclusion of the meeting, copies of two handbills purporting to emanate from the Western District Japanese Cotton Mills Strikers Committee were distributed among the attendance. One copy of each handbill is attached to this report with translation.

11月25日上午7时，九名自称是西北纺织公司第一、二厂工人代表的华人，以及两名分别名为 Siao Li ( 小 李 ) 和 Siao Zung ( 小 陳 )、自称是反日救国会代表的华人，以朱沂（江苏籍）和方覺庵（宁波籍）的名义，租下了天津路423号大上海旅馆的235、237和238号房间，目的是欢迎刑期届满出狱的工人。下午2时，三十一名工人抵达旅馆，其中25人属于西北纺织公司第一厂，6人属于西北纺织公司第二厂，他们声称刚刚获释出狱，并在237号房间举行了欢迎会。小李主持了会议，并表示被捕工人为了大家的利益而牺牲个人舒适的精神值得赞扬，所有工人都应以他们为榜样。在结束讲话前，他指示与会者于11月27日上午7时在中山路附近的周家桥集合，目的是前往上海市政府，请愿释放近期被中国当局逮捕的救国运动领导人。他还敦促与会者尽可能多带工人参加代表团。

会议结束时，向与会者分发了两份据称出自西区日资棉纺厂罢工委员会的传单副本。每份传单的副本及译文附于本报告之后。
