《每日新闻》：

红色工人被捕

自本地日本棉纺厂罢工爆发以来，杨树浦巡捕房一直竭力追查罢工的煽动者。通过该巡捕房警员及工部局警务处政治部的努力，获悉与共产党有关联的各救国会一直在这些罢工者背后非常活跃。
一名叫段奇林的中国男工在上海纺织公司被杨树浦巡捕房的警长上冈（Ueoka，音译）逮捕。据报道，此人是共产党员，在煽动者与罢工者之间充当联络媒介。警方搜查其住所时，发现了大量与罢工有关的宣传品。他于11月24日上午9时在第一特区地方法院被起诉，并被还押候审一周。

尽管工部局警务处政治部对一名在东兴棉纺厂外被捕的中国女教师进行了严密调查，但法院因证据不足将其释放。

《每日新闻》及其他本地日文报纸：

救国会领袖被捕

11月23日凌晨2时许，公安局会同公共租界及法租界警务当局，逮捕了全国各界救国联合会七名领袖。
被捕人员姓名如下：
1) 章乃器。
2) 沈儒（音译）。
3) 李公樸。
4) 王造時。
5) 沙千里。
6) 鄒韜奮。
7) 史良女士。
针对被告的案件聆讯于当日上午10时分别在第一和第二特区地方法院闭门进行。其中一两人获准保释，其余人由上海公共租界工部局警务处和法国警察羁押。下次聆讯将于11月25日上午举行。

《每日新闻》及其他本地日文报纸：

日华纱厂曹家渡工厂罢工

11月23日下午3时许，日华公司在曹家渡经营的各厂工人突然离开机器，在厂内举行示威。
公共租界巡捕和中国警察立即向各厂派遣了大量警力，并采取了预防措施。

November 23, 1936.
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER ... WE BRANCH）
Afternoon Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE STRIKE OF WORKERS OF JAPANESE COTTON MILLS

As a protest against the dismissal of six food contractors and the refusal by the mill management to grant the demand that operations be stopped at meal time, the 3,400 hands of the Kiwa Nos.1, 2 and 3 Cotton Mills in the Western district of Shanghai, who resumed work between November 20 and 21 on the advice of an official of the Bureau of Social Affairs and the Chief of the Zao Ka Doo Branch Bureau of Public Safety, went on strike again yesterday.
At 4 p.m. yesterday the strikers held a meeting at their quarters at which nine demands to be submitted to the management were discussed and passed.
After the meeting, the workers submitted the demands to the management, but without any result. At 6 p.m. they held a further meeting at which it was resolved to detail 18 representatives, 6 from each cotton mill, to call at the Bureau of Social Affairs at 8 a.m. November 23 and to request the authorities to open negotiations with the management over these nine demands. It was added that the hands would continue the strike should the management reject the demands.

Central China Daily News publishes the following article :-

The workers of Japanese cotton mills are badly treated; they not only have no days of rest, they have even to work at meal time. At the present time the Japanese cotton mills are making huge profits, but the Japanese capitalists have not restored the former scale of pay, but have, instead, increased the working hours. The workers went on strike.
The strikers have not submitted any conditions of a political nature; they have not resorted to any action that may be regarded as a menace to peace and order. For this reason, the Chinese policemen in this locality as well as the Chinese policemen in Chinese controlled territory are in sympathy with the strikers. The strikers are seeking assistance from the Chinese Authorities. At 6 a.m. November 11, some 1,000 strikers assembled on Huang Shing Road (黄兴路), carrying large banners in their hands bearing the characters: "The Appeal Group of Shanghai Cotton Mill Workers Going to the Shanghai City Government to Submit an Appeal". Their intention was to proceed to the Civic Centre. The Settlement Police detailed a large party of detectives and policemen to watch the movements of the strikers, while a large detachment of Japanese marines followed the strikers.
As the strikers were proceeding to Yingziangkiang (引翔港), policemen of the Public Safety Bureau stopped them going any further for fear of untoward incidents. The strikers appointed 13 representatives to call on the Chinese Authorities. They were received by an official of the Social Bureau, who advised them to exhort the strikers to remain calm pending mediation.

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

日本棉纺厂工人罢工

为抗议解雇六名伙食承包商以及厂方拒绝接受在用餐时间停止作业的要求，上海西区的琪华第一、二、三号棉纺厂的3,400名工人再次罢工。这些工人曾于11月20日至21日期间，在社会局官员及曹家渡公安分局局长的建议下复工。
昨日下午4时，罢工者在宿舍举行会议，讨论并通过了拟向厂方提交的九项要求。
会后，工人向厂方提交了这些要求，但未获结果。下午6时，他们再次举行会议，决议指派18名代表（每间棉纺厂各6名），于11月23日上午8时前往社会局，请求当局就这九项要求与厂方展开谈判。会上补充表示，若厂方拒绝这些要求，工人们将继续罢工。

《华中日报》刊登了以下文章：-

日本棉纺厂工人受到恶劣对待；他们不仅没有休息日，甚至必须在用餐时间工作。目前，日本棉纺厂利润丰厚，但日本资本家并未恢复以前的工资标准，反而增加了工作时间。工人们因此罢工。
罢工者未提出任何具有政治性质的条件；也未采取任何可被视为威胁和平与秩序的行动。因此，该地区的中国警察以及中国管辖区域内的中国警察均同情罢工者。罢工者正寻求中国当局的援助。11月11日上午6时，约1,000名罢工者聚集在黄兴路，手持写有“上海棉纺厂工人赴上海市政府请愿团”字样的大型横幅。他们的意图是前往市中心区。租界巡捕房派遣了大量侦探和巡捕监视罢工者的行动，同时一大队日本海军陆战队尾随罢工者。
当罢工者行进至引翔港时，公安局警察为防止发生意外事件，阻止他们继续前进。罢工者推选了13名代表去拜访中国当局。他们受到社会局一名官员的接见，该官员建议他们劝告罢工者在调解期间保持冷静。

November 23, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

This is a boom year for the spinning and weaving trade. The Japanese cotton mills should therefore accept the reasonable demands of the strikers so as to bring the strike to an end.

A large number of Japanese marines are maintaining special precautions along Yangtszepoo. Japanese tanks, machine gun cycles and motor cycles are patrolling the district. On November 10 when the workers of the Dah Kong (大康) Cotton Mill were on strike, Japanese marines opened fire, wounding Hsia Tsung Lin (夏寿林), a male worker of the Dong Shing Mill (同兴厂). A female worker of the Shanghai Spinning & Weaving No. 2 Mill was beaten and injured, while Sz Wei Ziang (施惠详), a male worker of the Dong Shing Mill was arrested. Such actions are an insult to the Chinese race.

The managements of Japanese cotton mills are sending many Chinese traitors to the district where workers live with the object of compelling hands to go to work; sometimes workers are even secured with ropes. These traitors also compel workers to advise other workers living nearby to return to work, otherwise the workers would suffer the fate of the workers Mei Sz Chuin (梅士钧) and Ma Ah Tao (马阿桃). The workers living in the quarters are so badly treated that they have to be taken on motor trucks by Japanese marines to their mills to work, while Chinese and foreign detectives and policemen as well as Japanese marines have to be posted outside the mills. In short, Japanese capitalists are employing every inhuman means to fight the strike.

The present strike must have been under contemplation a long time ago because of the oppression, exploitation and ill-treatment of the workers. The hands of other mills joined the strikers on their own initiative. The most serious defect in the present strike is the lack of organization. The strikers are even unable to elect responsible representatives to negotiate with the managements

If the present strike is simply an economic struggle, then our judgment has gone wrong. The strike is dealing a severe blow to the Japanese spinning and cotton mill trade, because, following the suspension of operations by the Japanese cotton mills, the price of cotton will rapidly increase, to the profit of Chinese commerce and industry.

Secondly, at this time of acute national crisis, when the whole nation is devoting its attention to the national salvation movement, such a strike is evidently a movement by brave Chinese workers for the emancipation of the Chinese race.

In view of this, the strike of workers of Japanese cotton mills deserves heartfelt support from the public, especially from the industrialists who should render every assistance to the strikers. We also hope that the Government will open negotiations with the managements of the Japanese mills in the interests of the strikers, while the public bodies throughout the country should form a Committee to Support the Strikers of the Japanese Cotton Mills.
pages.zh:
2
1936年11月23日。下午译件。

今年是纺织业的繁荣之年。因此，日本棉纱厂应当接受罢工工人的合理要求，以便结束罢工。

大量日本海军陆战队士兵在杨树浦沿线保持高度警戒。日本坦克、机枪摩托车及普通摩托车正在该区域巡逻。11月10日，当大康棉纱厂工人罢工时，日本海军陆战队开枪射击，打伤了同兴厂男工夏寿林。上海第二纺纱厂一名女工被殴打致伤，同兴厂男工施惠详被捕。此类行径是对中华民族的侮辱。

日本棉纱厂资方派遣许多汉奸进入工人居住区，目的是强迫工人复工；有时甚至用绳索捆绑工人。这些汉奸还强迫工人劝告附近其他工人复工，否则工人们将遭受梅士钧和马阿桃两位工人那样的命运。居住在宿舍区的工人受到如此恶劣的对待，以至于不得不由日本海军陆战队用卡车运往工厂做工，同时中外侦探、警察以及日本海军陆战队士兵不得不部署在工厂外围。总之，日本资本家正运用各种非人道手段来对抗罢工。

鉴于对工人的压迫、剥削和虐待，目前的罢工必定是蓄谋已久。其他工厂的工人也主动加入了罢工行列。目前罢工最严重的缺陷在于缺乏组织。罢工者甚至无法选出负责的代表与资方进行谈判

如果此次罢工仅仅是一场经济斗争，那么我们的判断就错了。这次罢工对日本纺纱和棉织业造成了沉重打击，因为随着日本棉纱厂停产，棉花价格将迅速上涨，这将有利于中国工商业。

其次，在这个民族危机深重的时刻，当举国上下都致力于救国运动时，这样的罢工显然是勇敢的中国工人为争取中华民族解放而进行的运动。

有鉴于此，日本棉纱厂工人的罢工值得公众，尤其是实业家的衷心支持，后者应向罢工者提供一切援助。我们也希望政府为了罢工者的利益与日本工厂资方展开谈判，同时全国各公共团体应成立一个支援日本棉纱厂罢工工人委员会。

November 23, 1936. 3、 Afternoon Translation.

The strikers of the Japanese cotton mills
in the eastern district of Shanghai have been forced to
resume work, but the workers of the Japanese cotton mills
in the western district have gone on strike. As a result

上海东部地区的日本棉纱厂罢工工人已被迫复工，但西部地区的日本棉纱厂工人则举行了罢工。由于丰田棉纱厂发生了一些骚乱，租界警务处和公安局调派人员镇压骚乱。不久之后，罢工者与警察发生冲突，许多工人受伤或被捕。随后，一队日本海军陆战队士兵被派往现场驱散工人。从罢工者受到日本军方和警察当局压迫这一事实来看，此次罢工不可能仅仅是工人与雇主之间的纯粹劳资纠纷。我们恳切希望全中国人民密切关注此次罢工并支持罢工者。

November 22, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Lin Pao (立報) and other local newspapers :-

STRIKE IN THE JAPANESE COTTON MILLS

As a result of mediation by Mr. Doo Yuet
Sen and Mr. Chien Sing Tse in collaboration with the
Chairman of the Japanese Cotton Mill Owners Association,
an agreement has been reached between the managements
of the Toyoda Nos. 1 and 2 Cotton Mills and their
employees. All the strikers have promised to resume work
to-morrow morning, November 23. The Japanese marines
posted in the cotton mills still remain, while members
of the Chinese and Settlement Police have been posted for
duty on various streets in the vicinity of the mills
as a precautionary measure.

Yesterday about 80% of the strikers of
Kiwa Nos. 1, 2 and 3 Cotton Mills, Robison Road, resumed
work following a promise by the managements that they
would adopt similar measures as other concerns in dealing
with the demand for an increase in wages.

It is also learned that the N.W.L. Cotton
Mill workers have decided to resume work to-morrow,
November 23.

On learning that the workers of the
Japan-China Cotton Mills, Jessfield Road, would join the
strikers of other cotton mills as soon as they had
received their wages, the managements, yesterday, requested
the Japanese Landing Party to detail additional marines
for duty within the cotton mills. Officers of the
Jessfield Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety were
posted inside the premises whilst others were on duty
in the vicinity of the mill. The situation in the Dong
Hsin No. 1 and Kung Dah No. 3 Cotton Mills remains the
same.

300 strikers of cotton mills in the
Western district of Shanghai intended to hold a meeting
in the People's Village, Chungshan Road, at about 10 a.m.
yesterday, but were frustrated and dispersed by police
of the Sin Zah Branch Bureau of Public Safety. They were
again dispersed when they planned to hold a meeting in
vacant premises near the suburbs of Tan Ts Wei Road, Chapei.

The situation in various cotton mills
in Yangtsepoo and Pootung remains normal. All mills
are working with a full complement of workers.

Lih Pao :-

CHINESE POLICE OF THE SETTLEMENT ASSAULTED BY JAPANESE

At about 8 p.m. November 20, a Japanese
named Shibata, residing at House No. 11 Morrison Road,
happened to pass by the corner of Haining Road and Woosung
Road in his private ricsha. As there were no lights on
the ricsha, Chinese Policeman No. 2992 approached to
inform him of the fact. However, the Japanese jumped
down from the ricsha and assaulted the policeman and
refused to be taken to the police station. The injured
policeman was conveyed to the Police Hospital for
treatment.

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

日本棉纱厂罢工

经杜月笙先生和钱新之先生与日本棉纱厂业主协会主席共同调解，丰田第一和第二棉纱厂资方与员工已达成协议。所有罢工工人均承诺于明日（11月23日）上午复工。驻扎在棉纱厂的日本海军陆战队士兵仍然留守，同时华警和租界巡捕已被部署在工厂附近各街道执勤，以防万一。

昨日，祁家宅第一、第二和第三棉纱厂（位于罗别根路）约80%的罢工工人复工，前提是资方承诺在处理加薪要求方面采取与其他公司类似的措施。

另悉，西北劳工棉纱厂（N.W.L. Cotton Mill，音译）工人已决定于明日（11月23日）复工。

得知极司菲尔路日华棉纱厂工人在领到工资后将立即加入其他棉纱厂的罢工行列后，资方昨日请求日本登陆部队增派海军陆战队士兵进厂执勤。公安局极司菲尔路分局的警官被部署在厂区内部，其他人则在工厂附近执勤。东信第一棉纱厂和公大第三棉纱厂的局势保持不变。

上海西部地区约300名棉纱厂罢工工人原定于昨日上午10点左右在中山路人民村举行集会，但被公安局新闸分局警察阻挠并驱散。当他们计划在闸北谭子威路（音译）郊区附近的空屋举行集会时，再次被驱散。

杨树浦和浦东各棉纱厂的局势保持正常。所有工厂均在满员状态下运作。

《立报》：

租界华警遭日本人袭击

11月20日晚8点左右，居住在莫利哀路11号的一名名叫Shibata（柴田，音译）的日本人乘坐私人人力车途经海宁路与吴淞路转角处。由于人力车上没有灯光，2992号华警上前告知其情况。然而，该日本人从人力车上跳下，袭击了警察，并拒绝被带往警察局。受伤的警察被送往警务处医院接受治疗。

D.C. (CRIM.)
November 21, 1936. Morning Translation.
7599

Sin 'an Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE STRIKE OF COTTON MILL WORKERS

In connection with the strike of workers
of local Japanese cotton mills, Mr. Doo Yuet Sen, Chairman
of the Shanghai District Association, has offered his good
offices to bring about an early settlement of the trouble.
The workers of the Toyoda and other cotton
mills in the Western district of Shanghai are still on
strike, but the situation in the various cotton mills
in the Eastern district has improved and no serious trouble
is expected.
Interviewed by our reporter yesterday,
a departmental chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs made
the following statement:- "With a view to securing a clear
knowledge of the situation and the attitude of both the
managements and the workers, the Bureau will despatch
officials to the Eastern and Western districts to make an
investigation. Instructions will be sought from the Chief
of the Bureau as to whether a further visit is to be paid
to the Japanese Textile Manufacturers Association in China
to discuss a settlement of the labour trouble."
Two days ago, the Police authorities of
both the Settlement and Chinese controlled territory
received information that those hands of the various
Japanese cotton mills who were still at work would go on
strike at 6 p.m. yesterday. Precautionary measures were
adopted especially in the Western district of Shanghai, such as
on Chung San Road, Brenan Road, Gordon Road, Robison Road
and West Soochow Road, where the Settlement Police and
the Bureau of Public Safety posted an additional number of
armed policemen; about 100 Japanese marines were posted
to guard the gates of the various Japanese cotton mills,
while an armoured car and a military truck were held in
readiness nearby. Strict precautionary measures were
also taken by the Police in the Eastern district.

After receiving the reports from the
Bureaux of Public Safety and Social Affairs, the Shanghai
City Government regarded the labour situation as being very
serious. The City Government will hold a joint meeting
in a few days with officials of the local Tangpu, the Bureau
of Social Affairs and the Public Safety Bureau to discuss
ways and means to settle the dispute.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE OPIUM SUPPRESSION MOVEMENT

Since the launching of the anti-narcotic
and anti-opium propaganda movement, more than 1,000 opium
addicts have surrendered to the Bureau of Public Safety
for treatment.
Mr. Yih, the chief of the 4th department
of the Bureau of Public Safety, in an interview with a local
representative of the Kuo Min News Agency yesterday, declared
that, acting on instructions received from the Opium
Suppression General-Directorate, the Bureau of Public Safety
will start an extensive propaganda movement in collaboration
with the various Tangpus, government organs and other local
public bodies.
The following methods of propaganda will
be used:- (a) Short, pithy slogans, (b) Cartoons, (c) Open
air speeches and (d) Beating of drums and giving of advice
to residents by word of mouth,

《辛安报》（Sin 'an Pao，音译）及其他本地报纸：

棉纱厂工人罢工

针对本地日本棉纱厂工人的罢工，上海特区公会主席杜月笙先生已出面斡旋，以期早日解决纠纷。
上海西部地区的丰田及其他棉纱厂工人仍在罢工，但东部地区各棉纱厂的局势有所好转，预计不会发生严重骚乱。
社会局一位处长昨日接受本报记者采访时发表如下声明：“为了清楚了解资方和工人的情况及态度，本局将派遣官员前往东部和西部地区进行调查。至于是否进一步拜访在华日本纺织制造商协会以讨论解决劳资纠纷事宜，将向局长请示指示。”
两天前，租界和华界警方均收到情报称，各日本棉纱厂仍在职的工人将于昨日下午6点罢工。特别是在上海西部地区采取了预防措施，例如在中山路、勃伦南路（Brenan Road，音译）、戈登路、罗别根路和苏州西路，租界巡捕和公安局增派了武装警察；约100名日本海军陆战队士兵被部署守卫各日本棉纱厂大门，附近还备有一辆装甲车和一辆军用卡车。东部地区的警方也采取了严格的预防措施。

上海市政府在收到公安局和社会局的报告后，认为劳工局势非常严峻。市政府将在几天内与当地塘埔（Tangpu，音译，指基层行政单位或地方组织）、社会局和公安局的官员举行联席会议，讨论解决纠纷的方法。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

禁烟运动

自开展禁毒和禁鸦片宣传活动以来，已有1000多名鸦片瘾君子向公安局自首接受治疗。
公安局第四处处长易先生（Yih，音译）昨日在接受国闻通讯社本地代表采访时宣布，根据禁烟总监署收到的指示，公安局将与各塘埔、政府机关及其他地方公共团体合作，启动大规模的宣传活动。
将采用以下宣传方法：(a) 简短有力的标语，(b) 漫画，(c) 露天演讲，以及 (d) 敲锣并通过口头向居民提供建议。

November 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

NIPPO

THE STRIKE OF MILL HANDS: POLICE ARREST 52 PERSONS

The strike of workers of Japanese
cotton mills is nearing an end. The red elements behind
the movement have become panic-stricken.
At 5.00 p.m. November 20, some
400 strikers assembled in the vicinity of the N.M.J. No. 5
Mill, formed themselves into two groups, and waited for
a watchman of the mill. As they failed to find him they
remained there until 6 p.m. and for half an hour they
held a demonstration against the day shifts who were
leaving the mill and the night shifts who were entering.
A report was made to Pootoo
Road Station and a party of police officers soon arrived.
13 female workers who were at the head of the demonstration
were arrested.
Another party of strikers
gathered in the vicinity of Ferry and Macao Roads at about
8 a.m. yesterday and as the situation became threatening,
police officers were despatched from Pootoo Road Station.
Upon their arrival, they effected the arrest of 40 male
and female workers. One of the arrested workers was
later released but the others were taken to the First
District Court for trial. Sentences ranging from 4 days
to 20 days were passed on them.
The majority of the strikers
are desirous of returning to work. In order to avoid
intimidation at the hands of agitators, workers often
attend their mills without cards or luncheon pails, while
those living in Chapel are taking a roundabout way by
making use of Sinza Road.
In the case of the trouble in
the No. 5 Mill, most of the participants declared that
they had been compelled to act.

《尼波日报》（NIPPO）

工厂工人罢工：警方逮捕52人

日本棉纱厂工人的罢工已接近尾声。运动背后的红色分子已陷入恐慌。
11月20日下午5点，约400名罢工者在内外棉第五厂附近集结，分成两组，等待工厂的一名看守人。因未找到该人，他们一直停留至下午6点，并对离厂的白班工人和进厂的夜班工人进行了半小时的示威抗议。
此事已向普陀路巡捕房报告，一队警官很快赶到。13名带头示威的女工被捕。
另一批罢工者于昨日上午8点左右聚集在渡船路（Ferry Road）和澳门路附近，由于局势变得具有威胁性，普陀路巡捕房派出警官。警官到达后，逮捕了40名男女工人。其中一名被捕工人随后获释，其余工人被押送第一特区法院受审。他们被判处4天至20天不等的刑期。
大多数罢工者希望复工。为了避免受到煽动者的恐吓，工人们往往不带工作证或饭盒前往工厂，而居住在 Chapel（查佩尔，音译，可能指某里弄或特定区域）的工人则绕道利用新闸路通行。
在第五厂的骚乱事件中，大多数参与者声称他们是被迫行动的。

November 21, 1936.

-2-

Kun, Woo Silk Weaving Factory - transient strike

A transient strike, commencing at 6.30 a.m. November
20 and terminating at 9.15 a.m. the same day was declared
by forty female day shift hands of the Kun, Woo Silk Weaving
Factory, a Chinese concern situated at Lane 215, No.4 Huichow
Road, as a result of one of their colleagues being assaulted
by an overseer. The strikers demanded that the overseer
should apologize to the female worker concerned and that
workers should not be assaulted in future. These demands
were accepted whereupon the strikers returned to work.

This factory employs a total complement of 94 hands.

Japanese Cotton Mills in Eastern District

The situation in the Japanese cotton mills in the
Eastern District this morning, November 21, is normal.

The day shifts of the Shanghai Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and
6 Cotton Mills are not operating this morning, owing to
the change over of shifts, which is the usual procedure.

The 23 female workers of the Shanghai No.3 Cotton
Mill who was arraigned before the Shanghai First Special
District Court on November 20, for being agitators (Vide
I.R. 20/11/36) were each sentenced to 5 days detention.

November 19, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

NIPPO (Editorial):

ANTI-JAPANESE FEELING IS BEING INTENSIFIED

The anti-Japanese feeling among the Chinese people is being intensified owing to the Suiyuan situation. At various places between Peiping and Shanghai, societies to support the Suiyuan forces have been organized. The situation resembles that created by the students movement in North China last year when anti-Japanese feeling was aroused throughout China. The present movement is worse because the unification of the front to resist Japan has been effected.

The strike of workers of cotton mills in Shanghai is one result of the movement. The strike has now taken on a political significance. Therefore, it cannot now be said that no anti-Japanese societies are active behind the strikers. The anti-Japanese United Front consists of communists, anti-Nanking and anti-Japanese elements. To the communists and anti-Nanking elements, the resistance against Japan is simply a means to create disturbances. They are the spearheads of the Anti-Japanese United Front, which is now moving forward.

Should the undesirable elements begin work seriously, the situation will be aggravated.

MAINICHI:

MOB ATTACKS CHINESE QUARTERS OF THE TOYODA COTTON MILL

After doing considerable damage in the No.2 Toyoda Cotton Mill, a mob of workers attempted to attack the No.1 Mill. When their attempt was frustrated, they rushed to the mill quarters in Jessfield Road and intimidated the female workers. After destroying an office in the mill quarters the mob went to No.12 Jessfield Road, the residence of Shch Lai Shien (石榴軒), an interpreter in the employ of the No.2 Mill, and did great damage. The attack took place between 11.40 p.m. and 1 a.m. Fortunately, Mr. Sheh was on duty at the mill at the time.

1936年11月19日。

《日日新闻》（社论）：

反日情绪正在加剧

由于绥远局势，中国民众中的反日情绪正在加剧。在北平至上海之间的各地，已组织起支援绥远军队的团体。目前的局势类似于去年华北学生运动引发的全国反日情绪高涨时的状况。当前的运动更为严重，因为抗日统一战线已经形成。

上海棉纺厂工人的罢工是该运动的结果之一。罢工现已具有政治意义。因此，现在不能说罢工者背后没有反日团体在活动。抗日统一战线由共产党、反南京政府和反日分子组成。对共产党和反南京分子而言，抗日仅仅是制造动荡的手段。他们是目前正在推进的抗日统一战线的急先锋。

如果不良分子开始认真行动，局势将会恶化。

《每日新闻》：

暴徒袭击丰田棉纺厂华人居住区

一群工人在对丰田第二棉纺厂造成相当程度的破坏后，试图袭击第一厂。当他们的企图受阻后，他们冲向极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的工厂宿舍区，恐吓女工。在摧毁了宿舍区的一间办公室后，暴徒前往极司菲尔路12号，即第二厂雇佣的译员石榴轩（Shch Lai Shien，音译）的住所，造成了巨大破坏。袭击发生在晚上11时40分至凌晨1时之间。幸运的是，谢先生当时正在工厂值班。

pages.en:
November 19, 1936.

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated Nov.18

THE STRIKES IN JAPANESE COTTON MILLS

To support their demand for an increase of pay,
the 7,000 workers of the Toyoda Nos.1 and 2 Cotton Mills,
Chung San Road (中山路), Western district of Shanghai, went
on a strike at 6 p.m. November 17. The strikers damaged
several window panes of the mills, seven weaving machines
and the furniture in the dormitory of the No.1 Mill.
At the request of the management of the Mills,
a squad of 120 policemen from the Bureau of Public Safety
and some 300 Chinese and foreign detectives and uniformed
men together with five Police vans from the Settlement
Police were detailed up to the scene to quell the disturbance.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party also despatched two armoured
cars and some 60 marines to the place.
A fight between the Police and the strikers
resulted in some 10 policemen and detectives being injured
from stones, whilst some 20 workers were assaulted and
injured by Police batons.
Before they left for the Civic Centre to submit
appeals to the Shanghai City Government and the Bureau of
Social Affairs, the strikers agreed to gather in Chung San
Road at 2 p.m. November 18.
Upon learning of this, the Bureau of Public
Safety and the Settlement Police detailed an extra number
of policemen and detectives to watch their movements.
After the workers of the Toyoda Cotton Mills
went on strike, eight Japanese marines were posted on duty
at the gates of the mills and two armoured cars were left
on the premises, whilst Chinese and foreign detectives as well
as uniformed men and officers of the Bureau of Public Safety
stood on guard at the gates and in the vicinity.
Motor cycles and armoured cars of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party are patrolling Brenan Road, Chung San
Road, Edinburgh Road, Gordon Road, Robison Road and West
Soochow Road.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE OPIUM SUPPRESSION MOVEMENT

With a view to propagating the movement for
the suppression of opium and other noxious drugs, the
Shanghai Municipality Opium Suppression Commission has issued
a manifesto advising all local opium and narcotic addicts to
come to their senses and undergo a voluntary cure of
their evil habit, because, commencing from next year,
capital punishment will be imposed upon all persons found
smoking or taking noxious drugs, such as morphine, cocaine,
heroin, red pills, etc. when they are arrested by the
authorities.
pages.zh:
1936年11月19日。

11月18日《大美晚报》

日本棉纺厂的罢工

为了支持增加工资的要求，上海西区中山路的丰田第一和第二棉纺厂的7,000名工人于11月17日下午6时举行罢工。罢工者损坏了工厂的几块窗玻璃、七台织布机以及第一厂宿舍内的家具。
应厂方请求，公安局派出120名警察，以及约300名中西探员和制服警员，连同工部局警务处的五辆警车被派往现场平息骚乱。日本海军陆战队也派遣了两辆装甲车和约60名海军陆战队员前往该地。
警察与罢工者之间的冲突导致约10名警察和探员被石块击伤，而约20名工人被警棍殴打致伤。
罢工者在前往市中心向上海市政府和社会局提交请愿书之前，同意于11月18日下午2时在中山路集合。
获悉此事后，公安局和工部局警务处增派了额外的警察和探员监视其行动。
丰田棉纺厂工人罢工后，八名日本海军陆战队员在工厂大门执勤，两辆装甲车留在厂区内，而公安局的中西探员、制服警员及警官则在门口及周边站岗。
日本海军陆战队的摩托车和装甲车正在白利南路（Brenan Road）、中山路、爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）、戈登路（Gordon Road）、罗别根路（Robison Road）和西苏州路巡逻。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

禁烟运动

为了宣传禁止鸦片及其他有害毒品的运动，上海市禁烟委员会发布宣言，劝告所有本地鸦片及麻醉品成瘾者醒悟并自愿戒除恶习，因为从明年开始，凡被当局逮捕时发现吸食或服用吗啡、可卡因、海洛因、红丸等有害毒品者，将被处以死刑。

November 19, 1936.
Date / /

-7-

At 9 a.m. to-day, November 19, 1936, three hundred
Chinese claiming to be representatives of strikers in the
Western District held a meeting on a piece of vacant ground
off Ping Ming Sing Tsung, Chung San Road, Chapei, when a
Chinese youth of the student type dressed like a worker
addressed the attendance and urged them to persist in the
strike. The meeting decided to place the following
demands before the mill managements :-
1) That an increase of 20% in wages be granted.
2) That Sunday be observed as a holiday.
3) That the working hours be fixed from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.
4) That an extra bonus of six days wages be granted to
each worker per mensem.
5) That no reduction in wages be made.
6) That extra leave be granted.
It was also decided that a delegation consisting of
four representatives of workers of each mill be sent to
the Shanghai City Government to make an appeal.
During the meeting the speaker claimed that he had
been sent by the Shanghai Various Circles National
Salvation Association to assist the strikers to secure
their demands, but refused to give his name.
This gathering was later dispersed by Police of the
Bureau of Public Safety.

今日（1936年11月19日）上午9时，三百名自称是西区罢工工人代表的华人在闸北中山路平民村外的一块空地上举行集会。一名身穿工人服装的学生模样的中国青年向与会者发表讲话，敦促他们坚持罢工。会议决定向各厂方提出以下要求：
1) 加薪百分之二十。
2) 星期日定为假日。
3) 工作时间定为上午6时至下午6时。
4) 每月发给每位工人相当于六天工资的额外奖金。
5) 不得减薪。
6) 给予额外假期。
会议还决定，由各厂四名工人代表组成代表团，前往上海市政府请愿。
集会期间，演讲者声称他是受上海各界救国会派遣来协助罢工工人争取诉求的，但拒绝透露姓名。
此次集会后被公安局警察驱散。

pages.en:
November 19, 1936
No. D
- 8 -
At 3 p.m. November 18, 1936, some 500 strikers
in the Western District assembled on Chung San Road and
discussed a suggestion of proceeding to the International
Settlement for the purpose of urging workers of all Japanese
mills to join the movement. This suggestion was overruled
by a male Chinese representing the Shanghai Various Circles
National Salvation Association, who stated that his name
was Huang Sing-ching ( 黄景 ), The latter urged
them to persist in the strike but to avoid creating
disturbances.
At 3.30 p.m. the same day, twenty strikers of the
Toyoda Mill, 200 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., held a meeting
in the Ping Ming Tsung ( 平民村 ), with Huang Sing-ching
presiding, when the following decisions were reached :-
1. That a committee entitled the "Japanese Cotton Mill
Strikers' Committee" be formed.
2. That fund soliciting groups be organized.
3. That picket groups be organized to protect the strikers.
4. That should police authorities interfere with the
strike, all strikers unite together and resist
such interference by force.

1936年11月18日下午3时，约500名西区罢工者在中山路集会，讨论前往公共租界以敦促所有日资纱厂工人加入运动的提议。该提议被一名自称代表上海各界救国会的华人男子否决，此人称其名为黄景清（Huang Sing-ching）。后者敦促他们坚持罢工，但避免制造骚乱。
同日下午3时30分，丰田纱厂（极司菲尔路200号，越界筑路区）的二十名罢工者在平民村举行会议，由黄景清主持，达成如下决议：
1. 成立名为“日商纱厂罢工工人委员会”的组织。
2. 组织募捐小组。
3. 组织纠察队以保护罢工工人。
4. 若警方当局干涉罢工，所有罢工工人应联合起来，以武力抵抗此类干涉。

A copy of a card bearing the following particulars
has been obtained by the Municipal Police in the Eastern
District :-

"Regulations governing the Election of Shanghai
Japanese Mill Labourers' National Salvation
Representatives.
(1) Aim :- Representatives are elected because we
are unwilling to become slaves without a country.
(2) Qualification :- All Chinese subjects working in
Japanese mills and their relatives are eligible
for election.
(3) Number :- There will be one representative for
each ten workers, or one representative in a
workshop where there are less than ten workers.
(4) Rule :- Voters and candidates are not allowed
to use their names in order to prevent traitors
from creating trouble.

Preparatory Office of the Shanghai
Labourers' National Salvation Society.
Representatives will
use this card for identification."

explained that the object of the meetin was to discuss
demands to be submitted to the management of the mills,
whereupon they were advised to submit the demands through the
Chinese authorities and to resume operations. The attendance
then decided upon the following demands :-
1) That an increase of 20% in wages be granted.
2) That the workers should not be cruelly treated.
3) That all dismissed workers be reinstated.
4) That a monthly bonus equivalent to 4 days' wages be granted
to all workers and that wages be issued twice a month
instead of once a month.
5) That half pay be issued to female workers during the period
of child bearing.
6) That Sunday be observed as holiday.
The Chinese Police promised to refer these demands to
the Shanghai City Government and advised those present at the
meeting to persuade all strikers to resume forthwith. The
meeting ended at 10.30 a.m.

Yangtszepoo Cotton Mill (British) - lockout lifted
The lockout in the Sackcloth Department of the Yangtszepoo
Cotton Mill, 1056 Yangtszepoo Road, which was declared on
November 17 following the strike of a number of workers
(Vide I.R. 17/11/36) was lifted on the afternoon of November
19, when the workers resumed operations at 6 p.m. pending nego-
tiations for a settlement of the dispute.
The situation in this department is normal, this
morning, November 20.

解释说，会议的目的是讨论向厂方提出的要求，随后警方建议他们通过中国当局提交要求并恢复生产。与会者随即决定了以下要求：-
1) 工资增加20%。
2) 不得虐待工人。
3) 所有被解雇的工人应复职。
4) 向所有工人发放相当于4天工资的月度奖金，并且工资每月发放两次而非一次。
5) 女工在生育期间应发放半薪。
6) 星期日定为假日。
中国警察承诺将这些要求转呈上海市政府，并建议与会者劝说所有罢工者立即复工。会议于上午10时30分结束。

At 11.45 a.m. November 17, about ten foremen of the

Toyoda Cotton Mills, 200 Jessfield Road, C.O.L. - workers clash with Municipal Police and Chinese Authorities

At about 6 p.m. November 17, the management of the Toyoda Cotton Mills, 200 Jessfield Road, C.O.L. detained in Mill No.2 a Chinese who was suspected of instigating other workers to declare a strike. This incident resulted in the day shift employees of both mills together with workers going on night shift proceeding to No.2 Mill, where they forced entry and smashed the machinery and fixtures. A party of S.M.P. and members of the Reserve Unit arrived on the scene and succeeded in driving the strikers across the Chungshan Road Bridge. Attempts were made to disperse the crowd but without success; the strikers using stones, iron bars and long swords to resist the Police. Two male strikers were taken into custody.

A large party of Police from the Bureau of Public Safety arrived on the scene and threw a cordon across the bridge.

11月17日下午6时许，哥伦比亚路（C.O.L.）极司菲尔路200号丰田棉纺厂厂方在第二厂扣留了一名涉嫌煽动其他工人宣布罢工的中国人。此事导致两厂的日班员工以及即将上夜班的工人前往第二厂，强行闯入并砸毁了机器和设备。一队工部局警察和后备队成员赶到现场，成功将罢工者驱赶过中山路桥。警方试图驱散人群，但未获成功；罢工者使用石块、铁条和长刀抵抗警察。两名男罢工者被拘留。

公安局的大批警察赶到现场，并在桥上设置了警戒线。

An economy movement has been started
by students of Fu Tan University under the direction of the
President and Vice-President of the university with the object
of raising funds to resist Japan.
All professors and students will put
their savings in an "Economy Box" and the amount will be deposited
in a bank every week.
The school authorities will issue
red and white orders to the professors and students; these orders
can be cashed later.
The entertainments by professors and
students will be cut down and the money saved will be put in the
box.

Nippo and other local Japanese papers.

RIOTING BY STRIKERS AT TOYODA NO. 2 COTTON MILL.

The strike situation in the Japanese
cotton mills took a turn for the worse yesterday. A riot took
place under the instigation of undesirable workers at the No. 1
and No.2 mills of the Toyoda Cotton Weaving & Spinning Co., No.
200 Jessfield Road.
It seems that at 6.00 p.m. November
17, some 30 male workers attended the No. 1 Mill and instigated
workers of all the departments to start sabotage. They
damaged a number of window panes. Operations were suspended
and the 1,500 male and female hands at work were ordered to leave.
At 6.40 p.m. the 30 male workers were joined by a number of out-
siders in the vicinity of Chungshan Road Bridge and attacked No.
2 Mill. They forced open the iron gate on Jessfield Road and
rushed into the No. 2 Mill which was then in operation. Entering
the nearest office they damaged the doors and windowpanes with
stones, bricks, poles etc; they also did considerable damage to
the machines.
A party of police officers from
Bubbling Well Police Station and the Reserve Unit as well as the
Indian Mounted Police turned up immediately upon the receipt of
a report of the trouble and co-operated with the men of the
Jessfield Road Sub-Station of the Bureau of Public Safety in
dealing with the situation. The 500 hands who were at work in
the mill left together with the rioters and assembled on the
other side of the road along the Soochow Creek and remained there
until midnight.

《日日新闻》及其他本地日文报纸：

召开会议讨论支援绥远
抗日部队

11月17日晚，在中国商会举行了一次会议，组织一个协会以支援绥远前线部队。约30位各界中国领袖出席了会议。

《每日新闻》。

复旦大学发起节约运动。

复旦大学学生在正副校长指导下发起了一场节约运动，目的是筹集资金以抵制日本。
所有教授和学生将把积蓄放入“节约箱”，金额每周存入银行。
校方将向教授和学生发放红白两色凭证；这些凭证日后可以兑现。
教授和学生的娱乐活动将减少，节省下来的钱将放入箱中。

《日日新闻》及其他本地日文报纸。

丰田第二棉纺厂罢工者暴动。

昨日，日本棉纺厂的罢工局势恶化。在极司菲尔路200号丰田纺织株式会社第一和第二纱厂，不良工人煽动下发生了暴动。
看来，11月17日下午6时，约30名男工来到第一纱厂，煽动各部门工人开始破坏活动。他们损坏了许多窗玻璃。生产暂停，正在工作的1,500名男女工被责令离开。
下午6时40分，这30名男工在中山路桥附近与一些外人汇合，袭击了第二纱厂。他们强行打开极司菲尔路的铁门，冲入当时正在运作的第二纱厂。进入最近的办公室后，他们用石头、砖块、棍棒等损坏了门窗玻璃；还对机器造成了相当大的破坏。
静安寺捕房和后备队的警官以及印度骑警队在接到骚乱报告后立即赶到，并与公安局极司菲尔路分所的警员合作处理局势。在厂内工作的500名工人与暴徒一起离开，聚集在苏州河对岸的路边，并一直停留到午夜。

pages.en:
November 18, 1936.    Afternoon Translation

Two squads were despatched from the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters to reinforce
the detachment stationed at the Toyoda Cotton Mill in
adopting precautionary measures. During the rioting
Mr. Shotaro Izawa of the No. 2 Mill was injured in the
face with a brick.

Red Elements Directing Riot

After the 30 workers of the Mill had
entered the No. 1 Mill, they closed the gate and prevented
the day-shift from returning home and locked out the
night-shift. While these workers were instigating the
workers of various departments, the Japanese employees
managed to open the gate and permitted the night-shift
to enter. Thus the plan of the agitators to cause a strike
was frustrated. The management suspended operations 30
minutes after this incident and ordered the workers to
clear out of the mill. Soon afterwards the No. 2 Mill
was stormed. There are at present 3,200 workers in the
No. 1 Mill, of which 800 are male workers. The No. 2
Mill employs 1,200 workers of which 150 are males.
The officials of the Toyoda Mills are
in receipt of information to the effect that undesirable
Communist elements have recently arrived in Shanghai; the
mill managements were conducting investigations to verify
the information, when the present incident occurred
unexpectedly. No demands have been submitted by the workers
and this departure from the usual procedure in labour
troubles is noteworthy. The mill officials emphasize
that it is Communists who had instigated the movement.
On the morning of November 17, officers
of the Bureau of Public Safety raided a house occupied by
a worker of the Toyoda Cotton Mill, who is a Communist,
to effect his arrest but he had already decamped. A
watch was kept on the premises by detectives. Later
a man claiming to be a student of Great China University
was arrested when he visited the house. He is being
detained at the Bureau of Public Safety at Nantao pending
further investigation.
At about 10 a.m. the same day, students
of the Great China University which is located on the
bank of the Creek opposite to the Toyoda Cotton Mill,
staged a demonstration, carrying banners inscribed with
the slogan "Support the Cotton Mill Strike". The
authorities concerned have adopted precautionary measures
against their activities.

Agitators Active

It is believed that an organized gang
of agitators are working behind the strike in the western
mill district. The nature of the strike is different from
that in the western district. During the morning and
afternoon of November 17, a mass meeting of strikers were
held at Macao and Perry Roads. About 3,000 persons
including radical students and lawless characters attended
the meetings.
After the meeting some of them proceeded
towards the N.W.K. No. 1 Mill and threatened workers who
were on their way to the mill. Others visited the workers'
homes and forced them to join the strike.

1936年11月18日。下午译文

日本海军陆战队总部派出两小队人员，增援驻守在丰田棉厂（Toyoda Cotton Mill）的分遣队，以采取预防措施。在骚乱期间，第二工厂的井泽庄太郎（Shotaro Izawa，音译）先生面部被砖块击伤。

赤色分子指挥骚乱

在该厂30名工人进入第一工厂后，他们关闭大门，阻止日班工人回家，并将夜班工人拒之门外。当这些工人煽动各部门工人时，日方雇员设法打开大门，允许夜班工人进入。因此，煽动者制造罢工的图谋受挫。事发30分钟后，管理层停止作业，命令工人离开工厂。不久后，第二工厂遭到冲击。目前第一工厂有工人3,200名，其中男工800名。第二工厂雇佣工人1,200名，其中男工150名。
丰田纱厂官员收到情报称，近期有不良共产主义分子抵达上海；厂方管理层正在进行调查以核实该情报时，此次事件意外发生。工人未提出任何要求，这种偏离劳资纠纷常规做法的情况值得注意。厂方官员强调，是共产党人煽动了此次运动。
11月17日上午，公共租界警务处（Bureau of Public Safety）警官突袭了一名身为共产党员的丰田棉厂工人所居住的房屋，意图实施逮捕，但该人已经潜逃。侦探对该处所进行了监视。随后，一名自称是大夏大学（Great China University）学生的男子在造访该房屋时被捕。他目前被羁押在南市（Nantao）警务处，以待进一步调查。
同日约上午10时，位于丰田棉厂对面河岸的大夏大学学生举行示威，手持写有“支持棉厂罢工”标语的旗帜。有关当局已对其活动采取预防措施。

煽动者活跃

据信，有一伙有组织的煽动者在西区纱厂罢工背后活动。此次罢工的性质与西区的罢工不同。11月17日上午和下午，罢工群众在澳门路（Macao Road）和倍开尔路（Perry Road）举行集会。约3,000人参加了集会，其中包括激进学生和不法之徒。
会后，部分人前往内外棉株式会社（N.W.K.）第一工厂，威胁正在前往工厂的工人。另一些人则走访工人家庭，强迫他们加入罢工。

pages.en:
November 18, 1936. Afternoon Translation.
( 3 )
Will the Strike Become a Political Struggle?
There are indications of the
present strike having the same characteristics of the
strikes declared during the May 30 Affair. It is
rumoured that a sum of $400,000.00 has been supplied
by the Comintern and a number of radical elements are
directing the strikers. Amongst these radicals are
several Communists who were arrested at the time of the
May 30 Affair and released during May and July this year
at the expiration of their sentences.
It is believed that the strike
will last some time and will spread to other mills. The
strikers have made no demands and are acting systematically.
Careful attention is being paid to developments in the
strike lest it take on political significance.
pages.zh:
1936年11月18日。下午译文。
( 3 )
罢工会演变为政治斗争吗？

有迹象表明，此次罢工具有五卅惨案期间宣布的罢工的相同特征。谣传共产国际提供了40万美元的资金，且有许多激进分子在指挥罢工者。在这些激进分子中，有几名共产党人是在五卅惨案期间被捕，并于今年5月和7月刑满释放的。
据信，罢工将持续一段时间，并蔓延至其他工厂。罢工者未提出任何要求，且行动有条不紊。正密切关注罢工事态发展，以防其具有政治意义。

November 18, 1936. Afternoon Translation

Lih Pao :

AN INCIDENT ON THE RIVER

As Mr. Kiang Shih (江樹), a staff member of the Public Works Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, was supervising the construction of a wharf at Yang Ka Doo (楊家渡), Poctung, at 4.30 p.m. November 16, two foreign river policemen with a Chinese officer passed by on patrol duty. The Chinese river policeman came up and asked whether the official had a permit from the Harbour Master. Mr. Kiang Shih replied that the work being done there came under the control of the Public Works Bureau, therefore no permit had been applied for.
The Chinese river policeman then ordered the suspension of the work. When Mr. Kiang Shih remonstrated, he was severely assaulted by the Chinese and foreign river policemen and was injured in various parts of the body. Mr. Kiang Shih was then forcibly dragged into the patrol boat and taken to the River Police Station.
Upon learning of this, officials of the Public Safety Bureau and the Sub-Inspector of the Chinese River Police Squad proceeded to the Station and secured the release of Mr. Kiang Shih who was afterwards taken to hospital for treatment.

Lih Pao:

MORE CHINESE COMMITTEEMEN OF FRENCH MUNICIPAL COUNCIL DESIRED

At a meeting held by the Executive Committee of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association in the French Concession yesterday, it was resolved that the authorities of the French Concession be requested to increase the number of Chinese committeemen of the French Municipal Council.
The meeting also passed a resolution that a general meeting of representatives of Chinese ratepayers be called on December 17.

The Modern World(現世界), a bi-weekly periodical, published the following article on November 16 :-

THE STRIKE OF WORKERS OF JAPANESE COTTON MILLS.

On November 9, about 15,000 Chinese workers in the employ of Japanese cotton mills in the Yangtszepoo and Western Districts of Shanghai and at Pootung went on strike and submitted 11 demands to their employers.
During the strike, Japanese forces in Shanghai were detailed to Yangtszepoo to maintain peace and order. When the workers of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill went on strike, the Japanese marines fired on the workers,

《立报》：

江上事件

11月16日下午4时30分，上海市政府工务局职员江树（Kiang Shih）先生在浦东杨家渡（Yang Ka Doo）监督码头施工时，两名外籍水上警察和一名华籍警官巡逻经过。华籍水上警察上前询问该官员是否持有港务长的许可证。江树先生回答说，此处进行的工程属于工务局管辖，因此未申请许可证。
华籍水上警察随即命令停工。当江树先生提出抗议时，遭到华籍和外籍水上警察的严重殴打，身体多处受伤。随后，江树先生被强行拖入巡逻艇，带往水上警察局。
获悉此事后，警务处官员及华籍水上警察队副督察前往警局，确保江树先生获释，随后他被送往医院接受治疗。

《立报》：

法公董局希望增加更多华人董事

昨日，法租界华人纳税会在执行委员会会议上通过决议，请求法租界当局增加法国市政委员会（French Municipal Council）中的华人董事人数。
会议还通过决议，定于12月17日召开华人纳税人代表大会。

双周刊《现世界》（The Modern World）于11月16日发表以下文章：

日本棉厂工人罢工。

11月9日，上海杨树浦、西区及浦东的日本棉厂约15,000名中国工人罢工，并向雇主提交了11项要求。
罢工期间，驻沪日军被派往杨树浦维持治安秩序。当大康棉厂（Dah Kong Cotton Mill）工人罢工时，日本海军陆战队向工人开火，

November 18, 1936.

wounding one man; his fate is unknown. One female worker of the Shanghai No.2 Cotton Mill was assaulted and injured with a wooden club by a Japanese policeman, while a worker named Sz Wei Ziang of the Dong Shing Mill is reported missing. The Japanese Landing Party attempted to compel the strikers of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill to resume work, but the majority of the strikers refused until their demands had been accepted.
The enemy is endeavouring to monopolize the various industries in China by means of his military and political influence. Our cotton weaving industry in North China has come under the control of the enemy and he is now doing his best to ruin the Chinese cotton mills in Shanghai. We request all far-sighted Chinese industrialists to render every support to the labour movement.
The workers of Japanese mills are ill-treated and oppressed to an intolerable degree. The managements reduce their wages, increase the working hours and prohibit them from talking in groups. The Japanese foremen assault and abuse workers at will while the Japanese marines visit the mills from time to time to make arrests and they often open fire on the workers; several had been reported missing.
The people throughout the country could render material support to the strikers by contributing one day's savings. We hope that our government authorities will open negotiations with the Japanese on the basis of the Factory Law.

Ta Kung Pao :-

YUNG PING PRIMARY SCHOOL TO STAGE PERFORMANCES

The Yung Ping Primary School (永平小学), Yung Ping Li (永平里), Markham Road, will give a big entertainment party at the Western Cinema (西海大戏院), Sinza Road, at the end of this year or on January 1, 1937. A play entitled "Under Gunfire" (炮火中) will be staged. During the party the Lei Tien Dramatic Society (雷電劇社) will stage two plays entitled "A Corner in the Metropolis" (都会的一角) and the "Smuggling" (走私).

Central China Daily News (Editorial) :-

THE DEFENCE OF SUIYUAN

The fighting in Suiyuan is not a local war; on the contrary, we should regard it as the final stage in the struggle for the existence of the Chinese nation. We should, with undaunted spirit, launch a counter-attack against the enemy. The officers and men defending Suiyuan are fighting courageously against the combined forces of the enemy, the bandits and "Manchukuo" soldiers. They are determined to smash the enemy forces. This is the spirit that will save the country.

致一人受伤；其下落不明。上海第二棉厂一名女工被一名日本警察用木棍殴打致伤，另有报告称东兴棉厂（Dong Shing Mill）一名名为Sz Wei Ziang（音译）的工人失踪。日本陆战队试图强迫大康棉厂的罢工者复工，但大多数罢工者拒绝，直到他们的要求得到接受。
敌人正企图凭借其军事和政治影响力垄断中国的各个行业。我们在华北的棉纺织业已处于敌人的控制之下，他现在正竭尽全力破坏上海的华商棉厂。我们恳请所有有远见的中国实业家全力支持劳工运动。
日厂工人遭受虐待和压迫，程度令人难以忍受。管理层降低工资，延长工时，并禁止他们聚众交谈。日本领班随意殴打和辱骂工人，而日本海军陆战队不时进入工厂进行逮捕，并经常向工人开火；已有数人报告失踪。
全国民众可以通过捐献一日储蓄的方式，为罢工者提供物质支持。我们希望政府当局能依据《工厂法》与日本方面进行谈判。

《大公报》：

永平小学将举行演出

位于马克姆路（Markham Road）永平里（Yung Ping Li）的永平小学（Yung Ping Primary School），将于今年年底或1937年1月1日在新闸路（Sinza Road）的西海大戏院（Western Cinema）举行大型游艺会。将上演剧目《炮火中》。游艺会期间，雷电剧社（Lei Tien Dramatic Society）将上演《都会的一角》和《走私》两部剧目。

《华中日报》（社论）：

绥远保卫战

绥远的战斗并非局部战争；相反，我们应将其视为中华民族生存斗争的最后阶段。我们应以无畏的精神，对敌人发起反击。保卫绥远的官兵正英勇抗击敌人、匪徒和“满洲国”士兵的联合部队。他们决心粉碎敌军。这就是救国的精神。

JAPANESE COTTON MILLS IN EASTERN DISTRICT - SITUATION

The situation in the Japanese cotton mills in the
Eastern District of the Settlement is normal this morning,
November 17.

At 1 p.m. November 15, 1936, a meeting took place
on a vacant ground in the vicinity of the Dah Doong Guild
( □ □ ), Yingsiangkian., Chapei, attended by twenty
Chinese claiming to be workers from various cotton mills
in the Settlement. One Siao Sze-ts ( □ □ □ ), carpenter
No.45 of the Dong Shing No.2 Cotton Mill, 2086 Yangtszepoo
Road, and two other Chinese presided. The following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1. That mill workers should appoint representatives.
2. That propaganda groups be formed for the purpose of
inducing mill workers to go on strike.
3. That picket groups be organized in order to protect
strikers and investigate the activities of those
workers of the mills who do not participate in the
strike.
4. That precautions be taken against strike-breakers.
5. That rice tickets be issued to the strikers, and that
preparations be made to register those workers at
present on strike.

CHINESE COTTON MILLS - SITUATION
- Sung Sing No.5 Mill - Increase in number of workers

The number of workers in the Sung Sing No.5 Cotton
Mill, 1316 Ward Road, has been increased from 1,265 to
1,750 (1,400 males and 350 females). This mill closed
at the beginning of February, 1935 and re-opened on
November 14, 1936.

东区日本棉厂 - 局势

11月17日上午，租界东区日本棉厂的局势正常。

1936年11月15日下午1时，在闸北引翔港（Yingsiangkian，音译）大东公会（Dah Doong Guild，原文不清）附近的一块空地上举行了一次会议，约有二十名自称来自租界各棉厂的华人工人参加。杨树浦路2086号东兴第二棉厂第45号木工萧四子（Siao Sze-ts，音译）及另外两名华人主持了会议。讨论并通过了以下决议：

1. 各厂工人应推选代表。
2. 成立宣传组，旨在诱导工厂工人罢工。
3. 组织纠察队，以保护罢工者，并调查未参与罢工的工厂工人的活动。
4. 采取防范措施，对付破坏罢工者。
5. 向罢工者发放米票，并准备登记目前罢工的工人。

November 16, 1936.

- 6 -

Japan-China Cotton Mills in Pootung (Japanese) -
activities of workers

On November 14, a notice purporting to emanate from
the Japan-China Branch of the Shanghai Municipality 5th
District Cotton Spinners' Union was found posted in the
vicinity of the Japan-China No.1 and 2 Cotton Mills, Pootung
Point. The Notice states that a joint strike had been declared
by workers of Japanese cotton mills in the Eastern District
of the International Settlement to enforce demands for the
increase of wages, and as a result, the managements had
granted a 5% wage increase. The notice further states that
the General Labour Union will be requested to negotiate
with the managements of the Japan-China No.1 and 2 Cotton
Mills, Pootung, for an improvement in treatment of the
workers. In conclusion, the poster advises workers not
to declare a strike.

On November 15 a petition containing the following
demands was submitted to the General Labour Union by
Zung Yah Zung (曾阿宗), an ex-worker of the Japan-China
No.1 Mill.

1. That workers be given a 20% wage increase.
2. That no workers be dismissed without cause.
3. That workers be allowed to have an hour for tiffin.
4. That the monthly bonus be restored to workers who do
not absent themselves from duty during the month
(This system was abolished in 1932).
5. That no extra work be given to the employees on Sundays.
6. That no workers be assaulted by foremen.

浦东日华纱厂（日资）——工人活动

11月14日，在浦东尖角附近的日华第一、第二纱厂周边，发现张贴了一份据称出自上海市第五区棉纺业工会日华分会的通告。该通告称，公共租界东区日资纱厂工人为迫使资方接受增加工资的要求，已宣布联合罢工，结果资方同意加薪5%。通告又称，将请求总工会与浦东日华第一、第二纱厂资方进行交涉，以改善工人待遇。最后，该海报劝告工人不要宣布罢工。

11月15日，日华第一纱厂前工人曾阿宗（Zung Yah Zung）向总工会提交了一份请愿书，其中包含以下要求：

1. 工人工资增加20%。
2. 不得无故解雇工人。
3. 允许工人有一小时午餐时间。
4. 恢复向当月无缺勤记录的工人发放月度奖金（该制度于1932年废除）。
5. 星期日不安排员工加班。
6. 禁止领班殴打工人。

N.Y.K. Cotton Mills - Meeting of Heads of Personnel
Departments
Between 10 a.m. and 12 noon November 14, a meeting
of the heads of the Personnel Departments of the nine
cotton mills of the Naikai Wata Kaisha in Shanghai was
held at the N.Y.K. Head Office, 931 Gordon Road when the

Chung Hwa National Goods Maintenance Association - Meeting
At a meeting held between 4.15 p.m. and 5.30 p.m.
November 15 at 51 Kao Fung Road, Nantao, nine committee
members of the Chung Hwa National Goods Maintenance
Association discussed and passed the following resolutions:-
1. That in view of the Administrative Yuan having decided
to require all government employees to buy national
goods, local national goods factories be notified to
compile lists of their production for distribution
among various official organs through the Chamber of
Commerce for reference.

with the Ministry of Industry.

11月14日上午10时至中午12时，在上海戈登路（Gordon Road）931号的日本邮船会社总部，召开了上海九家内外棉株式会社（Naikai Wata Kaisha，注：此处原文为Naikai，结合上下文及常见译法应指内外棉或相关日资纺织联合体，但依指令保留原文对应机构名逻辑，此处按当时语境通常指代日资纺织同业组织或特定公司群，鉴于后文出现N.W.K即内外棉，此处Naikai可能为OCR错误或特定称呼，暂按字面译为“内海”或保留关联理解，但根据历史常识及下文N.W.K，此处极可能指内外棉株式会社系统。然而指令要求不确定保留原文。经查证，Naigai Wata Kaisha即内外棉株式会社。此处Naikai疑为Naigai之误。为严谨，若无法确定则保留。但考虑到“N.Y.K Head Office”作为地点，且讨论的是Nine cotton mills of the Naikai Wata Kaisha，历史上内外棉在上海有多家工厂。此处暂译为“内外棉株式会社”，因为Naikai与Naigai拼写相近，且上下文均为日资纱厂。若严格遵循“不确定保留原文”，此处应标注。但鉴于后文明确出现N.W.K (Naigai Wata Kaisha)，此处极大概率为同一实体。为了通顺，译为内外棉株式会社，并在心中备注。等等，指令说“能确定的用当时通行的中文”。Naigai Wata Kaisha确定为内外棉株式会社。Naikai Wata Kaisha极可能是笔误。我将译为内外棉株式会社。）*修正：仔细查看原文，p499写的是Naikai Wata Kaisha，p498和p503写的是Naigai Wata Kaisha。这显然是OCR或原文拼写不一致。鉴于内外棉是当时主要日资纱厂集团，此处统一理解为内外棉株式会社。*

JAPANESE COTTON MILLS IN WESTERN DISTRICT - SITUATION

At 4 p.m. November 12, two hundred day shift workers
of the Spinning Department of the N.W.K. No.6 Cotton mill,
14 West Soochow Road, stopped work in order to enforce the
following demands :-

1. That a 10% wage increase be granted.
2. That no extra work be given to employees on Sundays.
3. That the workers be granted a daily half hour rest
period after tiffin.
4. That the dismissed workers be reinstated.
5. That the foremen be instructed not to assault workers.

The night shift hands (250) of the department joined
the strike at 6 p.m. the same day.

Following the strike, six workers were dismissed by
the management for being agitators. These dismissed
workers attempted to enter the mill this morning but were
frustrated, with the result that 450 employees of the
Spinning Department continue on strike.

In addition to these strikers, this mill employs
1,200 hands in other departments who are working as usual
this morning.

pages.en:
November 11, 1936.

-5-

At about 5 p.m. Nov.10, some 200 strikers appeared
outside the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, 195 Tengyueh Road, and
threw stones into the mill in an endeavour to incite the
workers of the Dah Kong Mill to join the strike. The crowd
was dispersed by the Municipal Police, and one person was
arrested. The arrested man will be brought before the
Shanghai First Special District Court this morning, Nov.11.

Following the arrest of the worker, about 300 strikers
assembled in the vicinity of Yangtszepoo Station and demanded
that the arrested person be released. These strikers were
eventually dispersed by the Police.

It is reported that strikers of various cotton mills in
the Eastern District are planning to detail pickets to the
vicinity of various mills now operating for the purpose of
inciting the workers to join the movement to obtain an
increase in wages. The most favourable times for these
activities according to the strikers are between 5 a.m. and
6 a.m. and between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. every day, when the
workers are changing shifts.

Shanghai Printing and Dyeing Factory - workers absent from
duty

About forty of the 100 day shift workers in the Fine
Yarn Department of the Shanghai Printing and Dyeing Factory,
(Chinese), 1382 Ward Road, absented themselves from duty
this morning, November 11, in order to enforce a demand for
a wage increase (Vide I.R. 10/11/36).

At 6 p.m. Nov. 10, one hundred female workers of the
department on the night shift turned up outside the mill
premises and demanded an increase in pay. The workers were
dispersed by police in the vicinity.

在该工人被捕后，约300名罢工者在杨树浦车站附近聚集，要求释放被捕者。这些罢工者最终被巡捕驱散。

据报，东区各棉纺厂的罢工者正计划派遣纠察队到附近各正在运营的工厂，目的是煽动工人加入争取增加工资的運動。据罢工者称，进行这些活动的最有利时间是每天上午5时至6时以及下午5时至6时，即工人换班之时。

上海印染厂——工人缺勤

位于华德路1382号的上海印染厂（华资）细纱部100名白班工人中，约有四十人于今晨（11月11日）缺勤，以强制要求增加工资（参见1936年11月10日情报报告）。

11月10日下午6时，该部一百名夜班女工出现在厂区外，要求增加工资。工人们被附近的巡捕驱散。

pages.en:
November 11, 1936.    Morning Translation.

NAIICHI

AMBASSADOR KAWAGOE MEETS GENERAL CHANG CHUN

Nanking, November 10.
At 3 p.m. November 10, Ambassador Kawagoe met General Chang Chun, Foreign Minister, at the latter's residence to continue the Sino-Japanese negotiations. The views of both Ambassador Kawagoe and General Chang Chun on some points have reached a stage of agreement but not enough for a final agreement. The meeting was terminated at 5.30 p.m. after they had fixed a date for the next meeting.
The Japanese Embassy has issued the following communique:-
Ambassador Kawagoe at 3 p.m. November 10 called on General Chang Chun, Minister of Foreign Affairs, at his residence and discussed the points which had been gone over on November 3 and 7 by Consul-General Suma and Mr. Kao Tsong Yu, a Departmental Chief in the Foreign Ministry. During the conference, Ambassador Kawagoe requested the National Government to give sincere consideration to the points in order to bring about a speedy settlement. The views of both sides were brought closer but not enough for final agreement. A further meeting has been arranged.

COTTON MILL WORKERS HOLD DEMONSTRATION: CLASH WITH POLICE

After their demand for an increase of 10% in their wages was rejected, the cotton mill workers in the Eastern District went on strike. Certain communists and members of national salvation associations are directing the strike. The strikers have turned down an increase of 5% offered by the managements of the Japanese cotton mills. Three Japanese cotton mills have suspended operations. The strike is affecting several Japanese dyeing factories for some 200 workers of these factories have presented a demand for an increase of wages. The workers of three Chinese cotton mills, the Ying On, the Sin Sir, and the Han Fong, went on strike prior to the Japanese cotton mill strikes. These three cotton mills are attempting to procure workers by increasing the scale of wages from 10 to 15%. On the night of November 9 a group of female workers of a certain Japanese cotton mill threw stones at the mill and came into conflict with the police on guard. The police arrested one female worker. A group of female workers held a demonstration in front of Yangtsepoo Station to secure the release of the arrested female worker, but were dispersed by the police.
Close attention is being paid to the strike because it is being directed by red elements. During the strike of the three Chinese cotton mills the Japanese cotton mills had to increase the workers' wages to prevent a strike among their mills.
pages.zh:
1936年11月11日。 晨间译稿。

内务省

川越大使会见张群将军

南京，11月10日。
11月10日下午3时，川越大使在外交部长张群将军寓所与其会面，继续进行中日谈判。川越大使和张群将军在某些问题上的观点已达成一定程度的共识，但尚不足以达成最终协议。双方确定了下次会面的日期后，会议于下午5时30分结束。
日本大使馆发布了以下公报：
川越大使于11月10日下午3时拜访了外交部长张群将军，讨论了须磨总领事和外交部高宗武司长于11月3日和7日讨论过的要点。会谈期间，川越大使请求国民政府真诚考虑这些要点，以便迅速解决争端。双方观点更加接近，但尚不足以达成最终协议。已安排进一步会晤。

棉纺厂工人举行示威：与警察发生冲突

在增加10%工资的要求被拒绝后，东区棉纺厂工人举行罢工。某些共产党员和救国会成员正在指导这次罢工。罢工者拒绝了日本棉纺厂资方提出的5%加薪方案。三家日本棉纺厂已停止运营。罢工也影响了几家日本染厂，因为这些工厂的约200名工人提出了增加工资的要求。英安、新狮和汉丰三家中国棉纺厂的工人在日本棉纺厂罢工之前就已罢工。这三家棉纺厂正试图通过将工资标准提高10%至15%来招募工人。11月9日晚，某家日本棉纺厂的一群女工向工厂投掷石块，并与执勤警察发生冲突。警察逮捕了一名女工。一群女工在杨树浦车站前举行示威，要求释放被捕女工，但被警察驱散。
由于罢工受到红色分子指导，正受到密切关注。在此前三家中国棉纺厂罢工期间，日本棉纺厂不得不提高工人工资，以防止其旗下工厂发生罢工。

At 6 p.m. November 10, no
workers turned up at the three Japanese cotton mills.
About 2,000 workers who are on strike surrounded other
Japanese cotton mills the hands of which were at work and

About 10 workers were assaulted and injured by stones.
A number of police officers and two riot vans from the
reserve units were dispatched to the scene from Yangtsepoo
and Yulin Road stations. The Japanese Consular Police
dispatched 10 officers led by Sub-Inspector Uasa. A
certain Japanese cotton mill employs 4000 workers, but two-
thirds of them are reported to have been prevented from
attending the mill. The cotton mill later used trucks
to convey its workers. The gate of the mill is being
strongly guarded.

November 10, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

HANDBILLS FOUND IN THE TUNGSHING COTTON MILL

Yesterday, a large quantity of
handbills issued by the representatives of the Japanese
Cotton Mill workers, was found in the W.S. of the Tungshing
No. 2 Mill. So far, the strikers have taken no violent
action and no outsiders are engaged in the strike. If
the object of the strike is to increase their wages, this
could be easily settled because the managements of the
Japanese cotton mills have decided to give an increase
of 5% although wages of the Japanese cotton mill workers
are higher than those of the Chinese cotton mills. Should
anti-Japanese agitators continue in their designs, they
will in all probability succeed in prolonging the strike.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE AND SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT

On November 6, the Northern
Branch of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street
Unions held a meeting in the Japanese school on North
Szechuen Road when it was decided to submit its resolution,
regarding the establishment of a special administrative
district, to the following:- the Japanese Consulate,
the Japanese military authorities in Shanghai, the Japanese
Residents Corporation, the S.M.C., and the Ministries of
Navy, Army and Foreign Affairs in Tokyo.
At 11.30 a.m. November 9, Mr.
Hayashi, Honorary Chairman of the Association, in company
with Mr. Kondo, Chairman of the Standing Committee of
the Association, and Mr. Hashimoto, Chairman of the
Northern Branch Association, called on Mr. Wakasugi,
Consul-General, to whom they presented the resolution and
gave a verbal report on the result of the meeting held
by the Association on November 6.

PEIPING MAYOR ORDERS DISSOLUTION OF STUDENTS
FEDERATION

Peiping, November 9.
On November 9, the Mayor of the
Peiping City Government issued an order to the Peiping
Students Federation and various other students organizations
to dissolve. It is believed by the general public that
the order will have no effect because nobody is qualified
to control the professors in Peiping who influence the
students. The professors hold a strong position in
political affairs. For this reason, the Charhar-Hopei
Political Council is unable to persuade the professors.
A number of professors, who are returned students from
Japan and are now well known to the public, have been
replaced by persons representing the Central Government.

1936年11月10日。下午译件。

《日日新闻》

在同兴棉纺厂发现的传单

昨日，在同兴第二棉纺厂的西区（W.S.）发现了大量由日本棉纺厂工人代表发布的传单。迄今为止，罢工者未采取暴力行动，亦无外人参与此次罢工。如果罢工的目的是增加工资，此事本可轻易解决，因为尽管日本棉纺厂工人的工资高于中国棉纺厂，但各日本棉纺厂管理层已决定加薪5%。若反日煽动者继续其图谋，他们极有可能成功延长罢工时间。

《每日新闻》

日本人与特别行政区

11月6日，日本街道工会联合会北部分会在北四川路的日本学校举行会议，决定就设立特别行政区一事向以下机构提交决议：日本领事馆、驻沪日本军方当局、日本居留民团、上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.），以及东京的海军省、陆军省和外务省。
11月9日上午11时30分，该会名誉主席林先生（Hayashi，音译）会同该会常务委员会主席近藤先生（Kondo，音译）及北部分会主席桥本先生（Hashimoto，音译），拜访了总领事若杉先生（Wakasugi，音译），向其呈交了决议，并口头报告了该会于11月6日举行会议的结果。

北平市长下令解散学生联合会

北平，11月9日电。
11月9日，北平市政府市长向北平学生联合会及其他各学生组织发布命令，令其解散。公众普遍认为该命令不会生效，因为无人有资格控制那些影响学生的北平教授。教授们在政治事务中占据强势地位。因此，察哈尔-河北政治委员会无法说服这些教授。一些留日归国且目前为公众所熟知的教授，已被代表中央政府的人士所取代。

November 10, 1936. Morning Translation.
JAPANESE COTTON MILL OWNERS HOLD CONFERENCE TO CONSIDER
STRIKES

At 4 p.m. yesterday the
Japanese Cotton Mill Owners Association held a meeting
at the Japanese Club to discuss and study the strike
situation in the three Japanese cotton mills in the
Eastern District.

On the afternoon of November 6
a section of female workers of the Shanghai Cotton Mill
went on a go-slow strike. On November 7 the situation
became normal. At 11 p.m. November 8 the workers of
the Tungshing No.2 Mill, the East China Cotton Mill
and the Shanghai Cotton Mill went on strike. Representatives
of workers of the Shanghai Cotton Mill and the Tungshing
Cotton Mill submitted a demand for an increase of wages.
The managements issued an announcement promissing an increase
of 5% and asked the strikers whether they would return to work
but so far no reply has been given by the strikers. For this
reason, the Shanghai Cotton Mill and the Tungshing Cotton Mill
did not open and no workers were allowed to enter. The East
China Cotton Mill received its workers. About 20% of the
strikers have returned to work.

日本棉纺厂主召开会议审议罢工事宜

昨日下午4时，日本棉纺厂主协会在日本俱乐部举行会议，讨论和研究东区三家日本棉纺厂的罢工局势。

11月6日下午，上海棉纺厂的部分女工实行怠工罢工。11月7日，局势恢复正常。11月8日晚11时，同兴第二棉纺厂、华东棉纺厂和上海棉纺厂的工人举行罢工。上海棉纺厂和同兴棉纺厂的工人代表提交了增加工资的要求。管理层发布公告承诺加薪5%，并询问罢工者是否愿意复工，但截至目前，罢工者尚未给予答复。因此，上海棉纺厂和同兴棉纺厂未开工，禁止任何工人进入。华东棉纺厂接收了其工人。约20%的罢工者已返回工作岗位。

7599

五家日本棉纺厂工人罢工

怠工运动未伴随暴力；警方监视局势；在棉花繁荣后要求加薪

昨日，上海日本棉纺厂的中国劳工骚乱蔓延，据公司官员估计，涉及五家工厂约8,000名工人。然而，据报道未发生暴力事件。
昨日清晨，杨树浦路同兴纺织有限公司（Dong Shing Spinning and Weaving Company）厂区约1,300名工人被拒之门外（lockout），此前据称煽动者于周日被逐出厂区，当时他们正进行怠工罢工。
位于华德路（Ward Road）的东洋纺绩株式会社（Tokwa Boseki Kaisha）旗下各厂的70%工人停止工作。厂方官员表示，男性工人并未在主要由呼喊组成的煽动活动中起主导作用。

要求大幅加薪

昨日清晨，所有日资工厂内分发了一些传单，要求加薪20%并改善待遇。这些传单是发给日资棉纺厂工人的。
昨日傍晚，同兴纺织有限公司和上海棉纺制造有限公司提出，凡在晚上6点前复工的工人均予复职，并保证全面加薪5%。
在华日本棉纺厂主协会的官员昨日上午在T. Funatsu先生（音译）的主持下，就局势进行了磋商。
上海《每日新闻》昨晚报道，上海公共租界警务处正在调查有关共产党及其附属的“救国会”是此次骚乱幕后推手的报告。

警方维持秩序

维持秩序的工作由上海公共租界警务处负责。昨日清晨派往杨树浦地区的日本海军巡逻队，因工人未表现出诉诸暴力的迹象而撤走。
继上周永安纺织制造有限公司、松星棉纺织有限公司和恒丰棉纺制造有限公司等华资企业约5,000名工人宣布怠工罢工之后，日资工厂出现了骚乱。据报道，鉴于当前纺织业的繁荣，厂主同意工人要求的10%加薪，昨日局势已得到解决。

Sixty night shift workers of the Reel Department and
200 of the Fine Yarn Department commenced a similar agitation
at 11.50 p.m. November 6, but resumed work at 1.10 a.m.

Lien Hwa Hosiery Factory - strike

The "tai-kung" strike declared by the 160 workers of
the Lien Hwa Hosiery Factory, Lane 580, 20 Rue Amiral
Bayle (Vide I.R. 5/11/36) developed into a strike on
November 6 following an unsuccessful effort to compel the
management to reinstate a dismissed worker. The strike
continues this morning, November 7.

上海总商会——致公董局关于香烟店执照费的函件

11月6日，上海总商会致函公董局（C.M.F.），鉴于目前商业萧条，请求法租界不执行增加香烟店执照费的规定。

劳工

上海棉纺织公司第四厂——短暂罢工

11月6日下午12时20分，位于雷路（Lay Road）585号的上海棉纺织公司第四厂细纱部的225名工人，为强制要求增加工资而停止作业。在资方承诺将其要求提交公司董事会会议讨论后，这些工人于下午2时30分恢复作业。

11月6日晚上11时50分，缫丝部60名夜班工人和细纱部200名工人开始了类似的骚动，但于今日凌晨1时10分复工。

联华袜厂——罢工

位于贝勒海军上将路（Rue Amiral Bayle）20号580弄的联华袜厂160名“台工”（tai-kung）宣布罢工（参见1936年11月5日情报报告），在试图强迫资方复职一名被解雇工人未果后，于11月6日发展为全面罢工。罢工持续至今晨（11月7日）。
